name: 3/4 sit-up
instructions: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind or to the side of your head. You will begin with your back on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Flex your hips and spine to raise your torso toward your knees.
At the top of the contraction your torso should be perpendicular to the ground. Reverse the motion, going only ¾ of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: 45° side bend
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and your arms extended straight down by your sides.
While keeping your back straight and your core engaged, in a controlled manner flex your upper body to one side, lowering your hand towards your knee.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Do it again on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: air bike
instructions: Lie flat on the floor with your lower back pressed to the ground. For this exercise, you will need to put your hands beside your head. Be careful however to not strain with the neck as you perform it. Now lift your shoulders into the crunch position.
Bring knees up to where they are perpendicular to the floor, with your lower legs parallel to the floor. This will be your starting position.

Now simultaneously, slowly go through a cycle pedal motion kicking forward with the right leg and bringing in the knee of the left leg. Bring your right elbow close to your left knee by crunching to the side, as you breathe out.
Go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Crunch to the opposite side as you cycle your legs and bring closer your left elbow to your right knee and exhale.
Continue alternating in this manner until all of the recommended repetitions for each side have been completed.

name: all fours squad stretch
instructions: Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand.
Use your hand to hold the foot or ankle, keeping the knee fully flexed, stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.
Focus on extending your hips, thrusting them towards the floor. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.

name: alternate heel touchers
instructions: Lie on the floor with the knees bent and the feet on the floor around 18-24 inches apart. Your arms should be extended by your side. This will be your starting position.
Crunch over your torso forward and up about 3-4 inches to the right side and touch your right heel as you hold the contraction for a second. Exhale while performing this movement.
Now go back slowly to the starting position as you inhale.

Now crunch over your torso forward and up around 3-4 inches to the left side and touch your left heel as you hold the contraction for a second. Exhale while performing this movement and then go back to the starting position as you inhale. Now that both heels have been touched, that is considered 1 repetition.
Continue alternating sides in this manner until all prescribed repetitions are done.

name: alternate lateral pulldown
instructions: Sit on the cable machine with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Lean back slightly and pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ankle circles
instructions: Use a sturdy object like a squat rack to hold yourself.

Lift the right leg in the air (just around 2 inches from the floor) and perform a circular motion with the big toe. Pretend that you are drawing a big circle with it. Tip: One circle equals 1 repetition. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
When you are done with the right foot, then repeat with the left leg.

name: archer pull up
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Activate your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
As you pull yourself up, flex one arm and bring your elbow towards your side, while keeping the other arm straight.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar and your bent arm is fully flexed.
Bring down yourself back down with control, straightening the bent arm and repeating the movement on the other side.
Alternate sides with each rep.

name: archer push up
instructions: Start in a push-up stance with your hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Straighten one arm straight out to the side, parallel to the ground.
Bring down your body by bending your elbows, while keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Push back up to the start stance.
Do it again on the other side, extending the opposite arm out to the side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: arm slingers hanging bent knee legs
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Activate your core and lift your knees towards your chest, bringing them as close to your elbows as possible.
Bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: arm slingers hanging straight legs
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your legs straight down.
Activate your core and lift your legs up in front of you until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold for a moment at the top, then bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: arms apart circular toe touch (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and arms extended to the sides.
While keeping your legs straight, flex forward at the waist and reach down towards your toes with your right hand.
As you reach down, simultaneously lift your left leg straight up behind you, maintaining balance.
Come back to where you began and do it again the movement with your left hand reaching towards your toes and your right leg lifting up behind you.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: arms overhead full sit-up (male)
instructions: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind your head and lock them together by clasping your fingers. This is the starting position.
Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Breathe out when performing this part of the exercise.
Once you feel the contraction for a second, lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: assisted chest dip (kneeling)
instructions: Adjust the machine to your desired height and secure your knees on the pad.
Grip the handles with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.
Bring down your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly, then push yourself back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted hanging knee raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.
Activate your core muscles and lift your knees towards your chest, bending at the hips and knees.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your abs.
Bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted hanging knee raise with throw down
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your palms facing away from you.
Activate your core and lift your knees towards your chest, while keeping your legs together.
Once your knees are at chest level, explosively throw your legs down towards the ground, extending them fully.
Allow your legs to swing back up and do it again the movement for your target rep count.

name: assisted lying calves stretch
instructions: Lay on your back with your legs extended.
Flex one knee and place your foot flat on the floor.
Using your hands or a towel, gently pull your toes towards your body, feeling a stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the stretch and do it again on the other leg.

name: assisted lying glutes stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.

Flex the hip of one leg, raising it off of the floor. Rotate the leg so the foot is over the opposite hip, the lower leg perpendicular to your body. Your partner should hold the knee and ankle in place. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to push your leg towards your partner, who should be preventing any actual movement of the leg.

After 10-20 seconds, completely relax as your partner gently pushes the ankle and knee towards your chest. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching.

name: assisted lying gluteus and piriformis stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your partner kneeling beside you.

Flex the hip of one leg, raising it off of the floor. Rotate the leg so the foot is over the opposite hip, the lower leg perpendicular to your body. Your partner should hold the knee and ankle in place. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to push your leg towards your partner, who should be preventing any actual movement of the leg.

After 10-20 seconds, completely relax as your partner gently pushes the ankle and knee towards your chest. Be sure to inform your helper when the stretch is adequate to prevent injury or overstretching.

name: assisted lying leg raise with lateral throw down
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms by your sides.
Place your hands under your glutes for support.
Activate your abs and lift your legs off the ground, keeping them straight.
While while keeping your legs together, bring down them to one side until they are a few inches above the ground.
Hold briefly, then lift your legs back to the start.
Do it again the movement to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: assisted lying leg raise with throw down
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms by your sides.
Place your hands under your glutes for support.
Activate your core and lift your legs off the ground, keeping them straight.
Lift your legs until they are perpendicular to the ground.
Bring down your legs back down to the start stance.
Simultaneously, throw your legs down towards the ground, keeping them straight.
Lift your legs back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted motion russian twist
instructions: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.

Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Your arms should be fully extended in front of you perpendicular to your torso and with the hands clasped. This is the starting position.
Twist your torso to the right side until your arms are parallel with the floor while breathing out.
Hold the contraction for a second and move back to the starting position while breathing out. Now move to the opposite side performing the same techniques you applied to the right side.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: assisted parallel close grip pull-up
instructions: Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height.
Place your hands on the parallel bars with a close grip, palms facing each other.
Hang from the bars with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.
Activate your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bars, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bars.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted prone hamstring
instructions: Lay face down on a mat or bench with your legs fully extended.
Have a partner or use a resistance band to secure your ankles.
Activate your hamstrings and lift your legs towards your glutes, while keeping your knees straight.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted prone lying quads stretch
instructions: Lay face down on the floor with your legs extended.
Flex your left knee and reach back with your left hand to take hold of your left foot or ankle.
Gently pull your left foot towards your glutes, feeling a stretch in your left quad.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release.
Do it again with your right leg.

name: assisted prone rectus femoris stretch
instructions: Lay face down on the floor with your legs straight.
Flex your right knee and reach back with your right hand to take hold of your right foot or ankle.
Gently pull your right foot or ankle towards your glutes, feeling a stretch in the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release and do it again on the other side.

name: assisted pull-up
instructions: Choke the band around the center of the pullup bar. You can use different bands to provide varying levels of assistance.
Pull the end of the band down, and place one bent knee into the loop, ensuring it won't slip out. Take a medium to wide grip on the bar. This will be your starting position.

Pull yourself upward by contracting the lats as you flex the elbow. The elbow should be driven to your side. Pull to the front, attempting to get your chin over the bar. Avoid swinging or jerking movements.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

name: assisted seated pectoralis major stretch with stability ball
instructions: Sit on a stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a stability ball with both hands and straighten your arms straight out in front of you.
Bring down under control the stability ball towards your chest, feeling a stretch in your pectoral muscles.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted side lying adductor stretch
instructions: Lie face down with one leg on a foam roll.
Rotate the leg so that the foam roll contacts against your inner thigh. Shift as much weight onto the foam roll as can be tolerated.
While trying to relax the muscles if the inner thigh, roll over the foam between your hip and knee, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.

name: assisted sit-up
instructions: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind your head and lock them together by clasping your fingers. This is the starting position.
Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Breathe out when performing this part of the exercise.
Once you feel the contraction for a second, lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: assisted standing chin-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing your torso and a grip closer than the shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, keep your torso as straight as possible while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position. Tip: Keeping the torso as straight as possible maximizes biceps stimulation while minimizing back involvement.

As you breathe out, pull your torso up until your head is around the level of the pull-up bar. Concentrate on using the biceps muscles in order to perform the movement. Keep the elbows close to your body. Tip: The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.

After a second of squeezing the biceps in the contracted position, slowly lower your torso back to the starting position; when your arms are fully extended. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: assisted standing pull-up
instructions: Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height settings.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Activate your lats and biceps, and pull yourself up towards the handles.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your back muscles.
Bring down under control yourself back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted standing triceps extension (with towel)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a towel with both hands behind your head.
Keep your elbows close to your ears and your upper arms stationary.
In a controlled manner straighten your forearms upward, squeezing your triceps at the top.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the towel back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted triceps dip (kneeling)
instructions: Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height.
Kneel down on the pad facing the machine, with your hands gripping the handles.
Bring down your body by bending your elbows, while keeping your back straight and close to the machine.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: assisted wide-grip chest dip (kneeling)
instructions: Adjust the machine to your desired height and secure your knees on the pad.
Grip the handles with a wide grip and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Bring down your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Push yourself back up to the start stance by extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: astride jumps (male)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex your knees and bring down your body into a squat stance.
Jump explosively upwards, extending your legs and arms.
While in the air, spread your legs apart and bring your arms out to the sides.
Land softly with your feet about shoulder width, bending your knees to absorb the impact.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: back and forth step
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width.
Step forward with your right foot, bending your knee and lowering your body into a lunge stance.
Push off with your right foot and step back to the start.
Do it again the movement with your left foot, alternating legs with each step.
Continue stepping back and forth, maintaining a steady pace.
Do it again for the desired duration or number of reps.

name: back extension on exercise ball
instructions: Place the stability ball on the floor and lay face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall or other stable surface.
Stance your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Activate your core and lift steadily your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: back lever
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Activate your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Flex your knees and tuck them towards your chest.
Lift steadily your legs up, keeping them straight, until your body is parallel to the ground.
Hold this stance for a few seconds, then bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: back pec stretch
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width.
Straighten your arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the ground.
Cross your arms in front of your body, with your right arm over your left arm.
Interlock your fingers and rotate your palms away from your body.
Lift steadily your arms up and away from your body, feeling a stretch in your back and chest.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then release.
Do it again on the opposite side.

name: backward jump
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex your knees slightly and jump backwards, pushing off with both feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, bending your knees to absorb the impact.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: balance board
instructions: Place a balance board in front of you.
Stand up on it and try to balance yourself.
Hold the balance for as long as desired.

name: band alternating biceps curl
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold the band with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and in a controlled manner curl one arm up towards your shoulder, squeezing your biceps at the top.
Bring down the arm back down to the start stance and do it again with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: band alternating v-up
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead, holding the band.
Activate your abs and lift your legs and upper body off the ground simultaneously, reaching your hands towards your toes.
As you bring down your legs and upper body back down, switch the stance of your legs, crossing one over the other.
Do it again the movement, alternating the stance of your legs with each rep.
Continue for your target rep count.

name: band assisted pull-up
instructions: Choke the band around the center of the pullup bar. You can use different bands to provide varying levels of assistance.
Pull the end of the band down, and place one bent knee into the loop, ensuring it won't slip out. Take a medium to wide grip on the bar. This will be your starting position.

Pull yourself upward by contracting the lats as you flex the elbow. The elbow should be driven to your side. Pull to the front, attempting to get your chin over the bar. Avoid swinging or jerking movements.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

name: band assisted wheel rollerout
instructions: Kneel on the floor and hold the handles of the band with both hands, palms facing down.
Place the band on the floor in front of you and stance your hands about shoulder width.
Activate your core and in a controlled manner roll the wheel forward, extending your body as far as you can while maintaining control.
Hold briefly at the furthest point, then in a controlled manner roll the wheel back towards your knees to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band bench press
instructions: Position a bench inside a power rack, with the bar set to the correct height. Begin by anchoring bands either to band pegs or to the top of the rack. Ensure that you will be position properly under the bands. Attach the other end to the barbell.

Lie on the bench, tuck your feet underneath you and arch your back. Using the bar to help support your weight, lift your shoulder off the bench and retract them, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Use your feet to drive your traps into the bench. Maintain this tight body position throughout the movement. However wide your grip, it should cover the ring on the bar.

Pull the bar out of the rack without protracting your shoulders. Focus on squeezing the bar and trying to pull it apart. Lower the bar to your lower chest or upper stomach. The bar, wrist, and elbow should stay in line at all times.
Pause when the barbell touches your torso, and then drive the bar up with as much force as possible. The elbows should be tucked in until lockout.

name: band bent-over hip extension
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at ankle height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet about shoulder width.
Step back to create tension in the band, while keeping your knees slightly bent.
Hinge at the hips and lean forward, maintaining a neutral spine.
Straighten your right leg straight back, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Bring down your right leg back down and do it again with the left leg.
Continue alternating legs for your target rep count.

name: band bicycle crunch
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your hands behind your head and your knees bent.
Lift your feet off the ground and bring your right knee towards your chest while simultaneously twisting your upper body to bring your left elbow towards your right knee.
Straighten your right leg while bringing your left knee towards your chest and twisting your upper body to bring your right elbow towards your left knee.
Continue alternating the twisting motion, as if you are pedaling a bicycle, while while keeping your core engaged through the whole movement.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band close-grip pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Stand facing the anchor point and take hold of the band with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Step back to create tension in the band, while keeping your feet about hip width.
Activate your core and keep your back straight as you pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the band back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band close-grip push-up
instructions: Place a band around your upper arms, just above the elbows.
Assume a push-up stance with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Flex your elbows and bring down your chest towards the ground, while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band concentration curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your legs spread apart and your feet planted on the floor.
Hold one end of the band in your hand and step on the other end with your foot on the same side.
Lean forward slightly and rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
With your palm facing up, in a controlled manner curl your hand towards your shoulder, while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your hand back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: band fixed back close grip pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a fixed point above you, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Sit down on a bench or chair facing the band, with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent.
Grip the band with a close grip, palms facing towards you.
Keep your back straight and activate your core.
Pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
In a controlled manner release the band back to the start, maintaining control through the whole movement.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band fixed back underhand pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point above your head.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the band with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Step back to create tension in the band, while keeping your arms fully extended.
Activate your core and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Pull the band down towards your chest, leading with your elbows.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
In a controlled manner release the tension in the band and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band front lateral raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold the band in front of your thighs with your palms facing down.
Keep your arms straight and lift the band up in front of you until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the band back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band front raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold the band in front of your thighs with your palms facing down.
Keep your arms straight and lift steadily them forward until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band hip lift
instructions: Lay on your back with your knees bent and feet planted on the floor.
Place a resistance band just above your knees.
Activate your glutes and core muscles.
Press your heels into the ground and lift your hips off the floor, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your hips back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band horizontal pallof press
instructions: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and—if possible—position the cable to shoulder height. If not, a low pulley will suffice.
With your side to the cable, grab the handle with both hands and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable.
With your feet positioned hip-width apart and knees slightly bent, hold the cable to the middle of your chest. This will be your starting position.
Press the cable away from your chest, fully extending both arms. You core should be tight and engaged.
Hold the repetition for several seconds before returning to the starting position.
At the conclusion of the set, repeat facing the other direction.

name: band jack knife sit-up
instructions: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind your head and lock them together by clasping your fingers. This is the starting position.
Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Breathe out when performing this part of the exercise.
Once you feel the contraction for a second, lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: band kneeling one arm pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point above your head.
Kneel down and hold the band with one hand, palm facing down.
Straighten your arm fully overhead, while keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Activate your lat muscles and pull the band down towards your side, bringing your elbow towards your ribcage.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: band kneeling twisting crunch
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height.
Kneel down facing away from the anchor point and hold the band with both hands, while keeping your elbows bent and close to your sides.
Activate your abs and in a controlled manner twist your upper body to one side, bringing your hands towards your opposite hip.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Do it again on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: band lying hip internal rotation
instructions: Lay on your back with your legs straight and a resistance band looped around your feet.
Flex your knees and bring them towards your chest, while keeping your feet together.
In a controlled manner rotate your knees outwards, away from each other, while while keeping your feet together.
Hold briefly at the end of the rotation, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band lying straight leg raise
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your legs straight and your feet together.
Place the band around the arches of your feet and hold the ends of the band with your hands.
By activating your abs, lift both legs off the ground until they are perpendicular to the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band one arm overhead biceps curl
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place one end of the band under your foot.
Hold the other end of the band with your arm fully extended overhead, palm facing forward.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, curl your forearm towards your shoulder, squeezing your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your forearm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: band one arm single leg split squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width and place a resistance band around your ankles.
Straighten one leg forward and rest the top of your foot on a bench or step behind you.
Hold onto a support with one hand for balance.
Flex your standing leg and bring down your body down into a squat stance, while keeping your knee in line with your toes.
Push through your heel to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch legs.

name: band one arm standing low row
instructions: Attach the band to a stable anchor point at waist height.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the band with one hand, palm facing inward, and step back to create tension in the band.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Pull the band towards your waist, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the band back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: band one arm twisting chest press
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height.
Stand with your side facing the anchor point and take hold of the band with one hand.
Step away from the anchor point to create tension in the band.
Stance your feet about shoulder width and slightly flex your knees.
Bring your hand holding the band across your body, towards the opposite shoulder.
While maintaining tension in the band, push your hand forward and away from your body, extending your arm.
In a controlled manner come back to where you began and continue for your target number of reps.
Switch sides and do it again the exercise with the other hand.

name: band one arm twisting seated row
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold the band with one hand and straighten your arm fully in front of you.
While keeping your back straight, pull the band towards your body by bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
At the same time, twist your upper body towards the side of the pulling arm.
Hold briefly at the top, then in a controlled manner release the tension in the band and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: band pull through
instructions: Begin standing a few feet in front of a low pulley with a rope or handle attached. Face away from the machine, straddling the cable, with your feet set wide apart.

Begin the movement by reaching through your legs as far as possible, bending at the hips. Keep your knees slightly bent. Keeping your arms straight, extend through the hip to stand straight up. Avoid pulling upward through the shoulders; all of the motion should originate through the hips.

name: band push sit-up
instructions: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind your head and lock them together by clasping your fingers. This is the starting position.
Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Breathe out when performing this part of the exercise.
Once you feel the contraction for a second, lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: band reverse fly
instructions: Attach the band to a stationary object at chest height.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold the band with both hands in front of you.
Keep your arms straight and lift them out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Bring down under control your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band reverse wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet planted on the floor.
Hold the band with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and wrap it around your fingers.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, with your wrists hanging off the edge.
In a controlled manner curl your wrists upward, squeezing your forearms.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your wrists back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band seated hip internal rotation
instructions: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Place a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Keep your knees bent at a 90-degree angle and your feet about shoulder width.
Activate your glutes and in a controlled manner rotate your knees outward, pushing against the resistance of the band.
Hold briefly at the end of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band seated twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and your back straight.
Wrap the band around your waist and hold the ends with both hands.
Activate your abs and in a controlled manner twist your upper body to one side, while keeping your back straight and your feet on the floor.
Hold briefly at the end of the twist, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Do it again the twist to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: band shoulder press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band under your feet.
Hold the band with your palms facing forward and lift your hands to shoulder height, elbows bent.
Press the band overhead, fully extending your arms.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the band back to shoulder height.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band under your feet, holding the ends with your hands.
Keep your arms straight and relaxed, and let the band hang in front of your thighs.
Activate your traps by shrugging your shoulders upward, lifting the band as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then bring down under control your shoulders back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band side triceps extension
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold the band with both hands, palms facing down.
Straighten your arms straight out to the sides, keeping them parallel to the ground.
In a controlled manner flex your elbows and bring your hands towards your shoulders, while keeping your upper arms still.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner straighten your arms back out to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band single leg calf raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width and place the band around the ball of your left foot.
Hold onto a stable object for balance if needed.
Lift steadily your left heel off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the ball of your foot.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your left heel back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the right leg.

name: band single leg reverse calf raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width and place the band around the ball of your foot.
Hold onto a stable object for balance.
Lift steadily your heel off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the ball of your foot.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heel back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other leg.

name: band single leg split squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width and place a resistance band around your ankles.
Take a big step forward with your right foot and a smaller step back with your left foot.
Flex your knees and bring down your body until your right thigh is parallel to the ground, while keeping your left knee slightly above the ground.
Push through your right heel to come back to where you began.
Do it again on the other side.

name: band squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, with the band placed just above your knees.
While keeping your chest up and core engaged, push your hips back and flex your knees to bring down into a squat stance.
Ensure your knees are tracking over your toes and your weight is in your heels.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push through your heels to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band squat row
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the band handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended in front of you.
Flex your knees and bring down into a squat stance, while keeping your back straight and chest lifted.
From the squat stance, pull the band handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band standing crunch
instructions: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the band with both hands and bring it up to your chest, while keeping your elbows bent and close to your body.
Activate your abs and in a controlled manner crunch forward, bringing your chest towards your knees.
Hold briefly at the top of the crunch, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band standing rear delt row
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band under your feet.
Hold the band handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended in front of you.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Pull the band towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band standing twisting crunch
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your upper back, crossing it in front of your chest.
Hold the ends of the band with your hands, while keeping your elbows bent and close to your sides.
Activate your abs and twist your upper body to one side, bringing your elbow towards the opposite knee.
Hold briefly, then come back to where you began.
Do it again on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: band step-up
instructions: Place a band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Stand facing a step or platform with your feet about hip width.
Step up onto the platform with your right foot, pushing through your heel.
Straighten your left leg behind you, keeping it straight.
Bring down your left foot back down to the ground.
Do it again with your left foot stepping up onto the platform.
Continue alternating legs for your target rep count.

name: band stiff leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your ankles.
Hold the band with both hands in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
While keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge at the hips and bring down under control your upper body towards the ground.
As you bring down, push your hips back and allow your knees to flex slightly.
Bring down the band towards the ground, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then activate your glutes and hamstrings to lift your upper body back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band straight back stiff leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your upper legs.
Hold the band with both hands in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
While keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent, hinge at the hips and bring down the band towards the ground.
Feel the stretch in your hamstrings as you bring down the band.
Activate your glutes and hamstrings to lift your body back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band straight leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your feet.
Hold the band with both hands, palms facing your body, and keep your arms straight.
Activate your core and keep a slight flex in your knees.
In a controlled manner hinge forward at your hips, while keeping your back straight and chest lifted.
Bring down the band towards the ground while while keeping your legs straight.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then squeeze your glutes and hamstrings to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band twisting overhead press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place the band under your feet.
Hold the band handles at shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
Activate your core and press the band overhead, fully extending your arms.
As you press, twist your upper body to one side, while keeping your hips stable.
Hold briefly at the top, then come back to where you began.
Do it again the press and twist on the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: band two legs calf raise - (band under both legs) v. 2
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and place a resistance band under both feet.
Hold the ends of the band with your hands for stability.
Lift your heels off the ground as high as possible, using your calves.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heels back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band underhand pulldown
instructions: Attach the band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the band with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Straighten your arms fully overhead, while keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Activate your lats and pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band v-up
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead, holding the band.
By activating your abs, lift your legs and upper body off the ground simultaneously, reaching your hands towards your toes.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your legs and upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band vertical pallof press
instructions: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and—if possible—position the cable to shoulder height. If not, a low pulley will suffice.
With your side to the cable, grab the handle with both hands and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable.
With your feet positioned hip-width apart and knees slightly bent, hold the cable to the middle of your chest. This will be your starting position.
Press the cable away from your chest, fully extending both arms. You core should be tight and engaged.
Hold the repetition for several seconds before returning to the starting position.
At the conclusion of the set, repeat facing the other direction.

name: band wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet planted on the floor.
Hold the band with both hands, palms facing up, and rest your forearms on your thighs.
In a controlled manner curl your wrists upward, squeezing your forearms.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your wrists back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: band y-raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold the band in front of your thighs with your palms facing inwards.
Keep your arms straight and lift them up and out to the sides, forming a 'Y' shape with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell alternate biceps curl
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width and hold a barbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms stationary and breathe out as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the barbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the barbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in as you in a controlled manner begin to bring down the barbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, alternating arms.

name: barbell bench front squat
instructions: Start by standing with your feet about shoulder width and the barbell resting on your upper chest, just below your collarbone.
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, while keeping your elbows up and your upper arms parallel to the ground.
Bring down your body down into a squat stance by bending at the knees and hips, while keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the squat, then push through your heels to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell bench press
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
From the starting position, breathe in and begin coming down slowly until the bar touches your middle chest.

After a brief pause, push the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out. Focus on pushing the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position at the top of the motion, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

name: barbell bench squat
instructions: Set up a barbell on a squat rack at chest height.
Stand facing away from the rack, with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex your knees and bring down your body down into a squat stance, while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Lift the barbell off the rack and step back, ensuring your feet are still about shoulder width.
Bring down your body down into a squat, while keeping your knees in line with your toes.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push through your heels to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell bent arm pullover
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with a barbell using a shoulder grip width.
Hold the bar straight over your chest with a bend in your arms. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your arms in the bent arm position, lower the weight slowly in an arc behind your head while breathing in until you feel a stretch on the chest.
At that point, bring the barbell back to the starting position using the arc through which the weight was lowered and exhale as you perform this movement.
Hold the weight on the initial position for a second and repeat the motion for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: barbell bent over row
instructions: Holding a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down), bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Tip: Make sure that you keep the head up. The barbell should hang directly in front of you as your arms hang perpendicular to the floor and your torso. This is your starting position.

Now, while keeping the torso stationary, breathe out and lift the barbell to you. Keep the elbows close to the body and only use the forearms to hold the weight. At the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a brief pause.
Then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell biceps curl (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Place your upper arms against the arm blaster, while keeping your elbows close to your upper body.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the barbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the barbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell clean and press
instructions: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand (or hook) grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.

Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the clean. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position.

name: barbell clean-grip front squat
instructions: With a barbell on the floor close to the shins, take an overhand (or hook) grip just outside the legs. Lower your hips with the weight focused on the heels, back straight, head facing forward, chest up, with your shoulders just in front of the bar. This will be your starting position.

Begin the first pull by driving through the heels, extending your knees. Your back angle should stay the same, and your arms should remain straight. Move the weight with control as you continue to above the knees.

Next comes the second pull, the main source of acceleration for the clean. As the bar approaches the mid-thigh position, begin extending through the hips. In a jumping motion, accelerate by extending the hips, knees, and ankles, using speed to move the bar upward. There should be no need to actively pull through the arms to accelerate the weight; at the end of the second pull, the body should be fully extended, leaning slightly back, with the arms still extended.

As full extension is achieved, transition into the third pull by aggressively shrugging and flexing the arms with the elbows up and out. At peak extension, aggressively pull yourself down, rotating your elbows under the bar as you do so. Receive the bar in a front squat position, the depth of which is dependent upon the height of the bar at the end of the third pull. The bar should be racked onto the protracted shoulders, lightly touching the throat with the hands relaxed. Continue to descend to the bottom squat position, which will help in the recovery.
Immediately recover by driving through the heels, keeping the torso upright and elbows up. Continue until you have risen to a standing position.

name: barbell close-grip bench press
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a close grip (around shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your middle chest. Tip: Make sure that - as opposed to a regular bench press - you keep the elbows close to the torso at all times in order to maximize triceps involvement.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your triceps muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

name: barbell curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at a shoulder-width grip. The palm of your hands should be facing forward and the elbows should be close to the torso. This will be your starting position.
While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second and squeeze the biceps hard.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell deadlift
instructions: Stand in front of a loaded barbell.

While keeping the back as straight as possible, bend your knees, bend forward and grasp the bar using a medium (shoulder width) overhand grip. This will be the starting position of the exercise. Tip: If it is difficult to hold on to the bar with this grip, alternate your grip or use wrist straps.

While holding the bar, start the lift by pushing with your legs while simultaneously getting your torso to the upright position as you breathe out. In the upright position, stick your chest out and contract the back by bringing the shoulder blades back. Think of how the soldiers in the military look when they are in standing in attention.

Go back to the starting position by bending at the knees while simultaneously leaning the torso forward at the waist while keeping the back straight. When the weights on the bar touch the floor you are back at the starting position and ready to perform another repetition.
Perform the amount of repetitions prescribed in the program.

name: barbell decline bench press
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and slowly lay down on the bench.

Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position. Tip: In order to protect your rotator cuff, it is best if you have a spotter help you lift the barbell off the rack.
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your lower chest.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up).
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

name: barbell decline bent arm pullover
instructions: Lay down on a decline bench with your head bring down than your hips and your feet secured.
Hold a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and straighten your arms straight above your chest.
Bring down the barbell behind your head in a controlled manner, while keeping your arms slightly bent.
Hold briefly, then lift the barbell back to the start by contracting your lats.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell decline close grip to skull press
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with your head bring down than your feet and hold a barbell with a close grip.
Bring down the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows, while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms to press the barbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell decline pullover
instructions: Lay down on a decline bench with your head bring down than your hips and your feet secured.
Hold the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Straighten your arms above your chest, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down the barbell in an arc motion behind your head, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Hold briefly, then go back the barbell to the start stance by reversing the motion.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell decline wide-grip press
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head bring down than your hips.
Grip the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Bring down the barbell to your chest, while keeping your elbows out to the sides.
Push the barbell back up to the start stance, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell decline wide-grip pullover
instructions: Lie down on a decline bench with both legs securely locked in position. Reach for the barbell behind the head using a pronated grip (palms facing out). Make sure to grab the barbell wider than shoulder width apart for this exercise. Slowly lift the barbell up from the floor by using your arms.
When positioned properly, your arms should be fully extended and perpendicular to the floor. This is the starting position.

Begin by moving the barbell back down in a semicircular motion as if you were going to place it on the floor, but instead, stop when the arms are parallel to the floor. Tip: Keep the arms fully extended at all times. The movement should only happen at the shoulder joint. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Now bring the barbell up while exhaling until you are back at the starting position. Remember to keep full control of the barbell at all times.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.
When finished with your set, slowly lower the barbell back down until it is level with your head and release it.

name: barbell drag curl
instructions: Grab a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing forward) and get your elbows close to your torso and back. This will be your starting position.

As you exhale, curl the bar up while keeping the elbows to the back as you "Drag" the bar up by keeping it in contact with your torso. Tip: As you can see, you will not be keeping the elbows pinned to your sides, but instead you will be bringing them back. Also, do not lift your shoulders.
Slowly go back to the starting position as you keep the bar in contact with the torso at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell floor calf raise
instructions: Place a barbell on the floor in front of you.
Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of the barbell, with your heels hanging off.
Hold onto a stable object for balance if needed.
Lift your heels as high as possible, using your calves to lift your body.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heels back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell front chest squat
instructions: Start by standing with your feet about shoulder width, toes slightly turned out.
Hold the barbell in front of your chest with your hands about shoulder width, elbows pointing forward.
Activate your core and keep your chest up as you bring down your body down into a squat stance, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Bring down until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push through your heels to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell front raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and lift the barbell forward and upward until it reaches shoulder level.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the barbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell front raise and pullover
instructions: Lie on a flat bench while holding a barbell using a palms down grip that is about 15 inches apart.
Place the bar on your upper thighs, extend your arms and lock them while keeping a slight bend on the elbows. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the weight using a semicircular motion and keeping your arms straight as you inhale. Continue the same movement until the bar is on the other side above your head . (Tip: the bar will travel approximately 180-degrees). At this point your arms should be parallel to the floor with the palms of your hands facing the ceiling.
Now return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the motion as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell front squat
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, bring your arms up under the bar while keeping the elbows high and the upper arm slightly above parallel to the floor. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids and cross your arms while grasping the bar for total control.
Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances described in the foot positioning section).

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor mainly with the middle of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell full squat
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder-width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting back with your hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell full squat (back pov)
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder-width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting back with your hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell full squat (side pov)
instructions: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder-width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting back with your hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell full zercher squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and toes slightly turned out.
Hold the barbell in the crooks of your elbows, with your hands gripping the barbell for stability.
Activate your core and keep your chest lifted as you bring down your hips back and down into a squat stance.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and your weight in your heels.
Bring down until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell glute bridge
instructions: Begin seated on the ground with a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise. Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lay down flat on the floor.
Begin the movement by driving through with your heels, extending your hips vertically through the bar. Your weight should be supported by your upper back and the heels of your feet.
Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

name: barbell glute bridge two legs on bench (male)
instructions: Begin seated on the ground with a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise. Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lay down flat on the floor.
Begin the movement by driving through with your heels, extending your hips vertically through the bar. Your weight should be supported by your upper back and the heels of your feet.
Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

name: barbell good morning
instructions: Begin with a bar on a rack at shoulder height. Rack the bar across the rear of your shoulders as you would a power squat, not on top of your shoulders. Keep your back tight, shoulder blades pinched together, and your knees slightly bent. Step back from the rack.
Begin by bending at the hips, moving them back as you bend over to near parallel. Keep your back arched and your cervical spine in proper alignment.
Reverse the motion by extending through the hips with your glutes and hamstrings. Continue until you have returned to the starting position.

name: barbell guillotine bench press
instructions: Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over your neck with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, bring the bar down slowly until it is about 1 inch from your neck.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

name: barbell hack squat
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a barbell behind you at arms length and your feet at shoulder width. Tip: A shoulder width grip is best with the palms of your hands facing back. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your head and eyes up and back straight, squat until your upper thighs are parallel to the floor. Breathe in as you slowly go down.
Pressing mainly with the heel of the foot and squeezing the thighs, go back up as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: barbell high bar squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, toes slightly turned out.
Place the barbell on your upper back, resting it on your traps.
Activate your core and keep your chest up as you begin to squat down, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Bring down yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Drive through your heels to stand back up, extending your hips and knees.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell incline bench press
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench. Using a medium-width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on you upper chest.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: it should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

name: barbell incline close grip bench press
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lay down on the bench with your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than about shoulder width.
Unrack the barbell and bring down it in a controlled manner towards your chest, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold briefly when the barbell touches your chest.
Push the barbell back up to the start stance, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell incline reverse-grip press
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lay back on the bench and grip the barbell with a reverse grip, hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Unrack the barbell and bring down it towards your upper chest, while keeping your elbows tucked in.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: barbell incline row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lay face down on the bench with your chest against the pad and your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
