To perform the movement, tuck the knees toward your chest by flexing the hips and knees. Following this, extend your legs directly above you so that they are perpendicular to the ground. Rotate and elevate your pelvis to raise your glutes from the floor.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

name: box jump down with one leg stabilization
instructions: Stand in front of a box or platform with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex your knees and jump onto the box, landing softly with one foot on the box and the other foot hanging off the edge.
Stabilize yourself on the box with the foot that is on it, while keeping the other foot off the ground.
Hold this stance for a few seconds, by activating your calf muscles to keep balance.
In a controlled manner step down with the foot that is on the box, returning to the start stance.
Do it again the exercise with the other leg.

name: bridge - mountain climber (cross body)
instructions: Start in a high plank stance with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Activate your core and lift your right foot off the ground, bringing your right knee towards your left elbow.
Go back your right foot to the start stance and do it again the movement with your left foot towards your right elbow.
Continue alternating sides, moving at a controlled pace.
Keep your hips level and avoid lifting your hips too high or sagging them too low.
Keep a steady breathing pattern during the exercise.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: burpee
instructions: Start in a standing stance with your feet about shoulder width.
Bring down your body into a squat stance by bending your knees and placing your hands on the floor in front of you.
Kick your feet back into a push-up stance.
Do a push-up, while keeping your body in a straight line.
Jump your feet back into the squat stance.
Jump up explosively, reaching your arms overhead.
Land softly and immediately bring down back into a squat stance to begin the next rep.

name: butt-ups
instructions: Begin a pushup position but with your elbows on the ground and resting on your forearms. Your arms should be bent at a 90 degree angle.
Arch your back slightly out rather than keeping your back completely straight.

Raise your glutes toward the ceiling, squeezing your abs tightly to close the distance between your ribcage and hips. The end result will be that you'll end up in a high bridge position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Lower back down slowly to your starting position as you breathe in. Tip: Don't let your back sag downwards.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: butterfly yoga pose
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back flat on the pad.
Take hold of the handles. Tip: Your upper arms should be positioned parallel to the floor; adjust the machine accordingly. This will be your starting position.
Push the handles together slowly as you squeeze your chest in the middle. Breathe out during this part of the motion and hold the contraction for a second.
Return back to the starting position slowly as you inhale until your chest muscles are fully stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable alternate shoulder press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and grip the handles of the cable machine with an overhand grip.
Stance your hands at shoulder height, with your palms facing forward.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight.
Press one handle up and forward until your arm is fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the handle back to the start.
Do it again with the other arm.
Alternate between arms for your target rep count.

name: cable alternate triceps extension
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the cable handle with your right hand and bring your arm up so that your upper arm is parallel to the ground and your elbow is bent at a 90-degree angle.
Keep your upper arm stationary and straighten your forearm backward, fully straightening your arm.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Do it again with your left arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: cable assisted inverse leg curl
instructions: Adjust the cable machine so that the ankle attachment is at the lowest setting.
Lay face down on the bench with your legs straight and the ankle attachment secured to your ankles.
Hold onto the handles of the bench for stability.
While keeping your upper body stationary, breathe out and curl your legs up towards your glutes by flexing your knees.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your hamstrings.
Breathe in and bring down under control your legs back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable bar lateral pulldown
instructions: Adjust the cable pulley to a high stance and attach a straight bar.
Sit facing the cable machine with your feet planted on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up, maintaining a slight arch in your bring down back.
Pull the bar down towards your chest, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner go back the bar to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable bench press
instructions: Adjust the cable machine to chest height and attach the handles.
Stand facing away from the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and step forward to create tension in the cables.
Stance your feet firmly on the floor and activate your core.
Flex your elbows and bring your hands to shoulder level, while keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward, extending your arms fully in front of you.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner reverse the movement, bringing your hands back to shoulder level.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable close grip curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary during the exercise.
Breathe out and curl the bar up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the bar back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable concentration curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet flat on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Hold the cable handle with an underhand grip and rest your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and curl the cable handle towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then breathe in and bring down under control the cable handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable concentration extension (on knee)
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your knees bent and feet planted on the floor.
Hold the cable handle with your right hand and place your elbow on the inside of your right knee.
Straighten your arm fully, while keeping your elbow stationary and close to your knee.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable cross-over lateral pulldown
instructions: Attach a cable handle to each side of a cable machine at shoulder height.
Stand in the middle of the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and step back to create tension in the cables.
Lean forward slightly from the hips, while keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Pull the handles down and across your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable cross-over revers fly
instructions: Attach a D-handle to each low pulley cable and stand in the middle of the cable crossover machine.
Grip the handles with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and take a step forward, positioning your feet about shoulder width.
Flex your knees slightly and lean forward at the waist, while keeping your back straight and your abs engaged.
With your arms extended out to the sides and slightly bent at the elbows, breathe out and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the cables back and upward in a reverse fly motion.
Hold briefly at the peak contraction, then breathe in and in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable cross-over variation
instructions: Adjust the cable pulleys to chest height.
Stand in the center of the cable machine with one foot in front of the other.
Grip the handles with your palms facing down and your arms extended out to the sides.
Take a step forward, while keeping your arms slightly bent.
With a slight flex in your elbows, bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner go back your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable curl
instructions: Stand between a couple of high pulleys and grab a handle in each arm. Position your upper arms in a way that they are parallel to the floor with the palms of your hands facing you. This will be your starting position.

Curl the handles towards you until they are next to your ears. Make sure that as you do so you flex your biceps and exhale. The upper arms should remain stationary and only the forearms should move. Hold for a second in the contracted position as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly bring back the arms to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable deadlift
instructions: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight. Stand directly in between the uprights.
To begin, squat down be flexing your hips and knees until you can reach the handles.
After grasping them, begin your ascent. Driving through your heels extend your hips and knees keeping your hands hanging at your side. Keep your head and chest up throughout the movement.
After reaching a full standing position, Return to the starting position and repeat.

name: cable decline fly
instructions: Adjust the cable machine to a decline stance.
Stand facing away from the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the handles with your palms facing forward and your arms extended straight out in front of you.
Keeping a slight flex in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides in a steady motion.
Hold briefly at the fully extended stance, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable decline one arm press
instructions: Adjust the cable machine to a decline stance.
Stand facing away from the machine and take hold of the handle with one hand.
Stance yourself with your back against the decline bench and your arm extended straight in front of you.
Flex your elbow and bring down the handle towards your chest while while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push the handle back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable decline press
instructions: Adjust the cable machine to a decline stance.
Sit on the decline bench facing the cable machine.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and stance them at chest level.
Keep your feet planted on the floor and your back firmly against the bench.
Breathe out and push the handles away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Hold briefly at the end of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner go back the handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable decline seated wide-grip row
instructions: Sit on the decline bench facing the cable machine with your feet securely placed on the footrests.
Grip the cable attachment with a wide overhand grip, palms facing down.
Lean back slightly, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable towards your bring down chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the contraction, then in a controlled manner release the cable back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable drag curl
instructions: Grab a barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing forward) and get your elbows close to your torso and back. This will be your starting position.

As you exhale, curl the bar up while keeping the elbows to the back as you "Drag" the bar up by keeping it in contact with your torso. Tip: As you can see, you will not be keeping the elbows pinned to your sides, but instead you will be bringing them back. Also, do not lift your shoulders.
Slowly go back to the starting position as you keep the bar in contact with the torso at all times.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable floor seated wide-grip row
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your back straight.
Attach a cable handle to a low pulley and stance the cable machine behind you.
Grip the handle with a wide overhand grip, palms facing down.
Lean back slightly, while keeping your back straight and your chest lifted.
Pull the handle towards your waist, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable forward raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and your knees slightly bent.
Hold the cable handle with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and your arms fully extended in front of you.
While keeping your arms straight, lift the cable handle up to shoulder level.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the cable handle back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable front raise
instructions: Select the weight on a low pulley machine and grasp the single hand cable attachment that is attached to the low pulley with your left hand.

Face away from the pulley and put your arm straight down with the hand cable attachment in front of your thighs at arms' length with the palms of the hand facing your thighs. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the left arm to the front with a slight bend on the elbow and the palms of the hand always faces down. Continue to go up until you arm is slightly above parallel to the floor. Exhale as you execute this portion of the movement and pause for a second at the top.
Now as you inhale lower the arm back down slowly to the starting position.
Once all of the recommended amount of repetitions have been performed for this arm, switch arms and perform the exercise with the right one.

name: cable front shoulder raise
instructions: Relax your arms to your sides and raise your shoulders up toward your ears, then back down.

name: cable hammer curl (with rope)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet about shoulder width and a slight flex in your knees.
Hold the cable rope attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing each other, and your arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the cable rope attachment until your biceps are fully contracted and the rope is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the cable rope attachment back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable high pulley overhead tricep extension
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand facing away from the machine.
Grip the rope with both hands and straighten your arms overhead.
Keep your elbows close to your head and your upper arms stationary.
Bring down under control the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable high row (kneeling)
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a cable machine at chest height.
Kneel down in front of the cable machine and take hold of the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Sit back on your heels, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the bar towards your upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the bar back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable hip adduction
instructions: Stand in front of a low pulley facing forward with one leg next to the pulley and the other one away.
Attach the ankle cuff to the cable and also to the ankle of the leg that is next to the pulley.
Now step out and away from the stack with a wide stance and grasp the bar of the pulley system.
Stand on the foot that does not have the ankle cuff (the far foot) and allow the leg with the cuff to be pulled towards the low pulley. This will be your starting position.
Now perform the movement by moving the leg with the ankle cuff in front of the far leg by using the inner thighs to abduct the hip. Breathe out during this portion of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then repeat the same movement with the opposite leg.

name: cable incline bench press
instructions: Adjust the bench to a 45-degree incline.
Attach the cable handles to the high pulleys.
Sit on the bench facing the cable machine with your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and bring them to shoulder height.
Push the handles forward and upward until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable incline bench row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle and attach a cable handle to the low pulley.
Sit on the bench facing the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the cable handle with an overhand grip and straighten your arms fully in front of you.
Lean forward from your hips while while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable handle towards your chest by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement, then in a controlled manner straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable incline fly
instructions: Adjust the cable machine to a low stance and attach the handles.
Sit on an incline bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and straighten your arms straight out in front of you.
Keeping a slight flex in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides in a steady motion.
Hold briefly at the fully extended stance, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable incline fly (on stability ball)
instructions: Set up a stability ball at an incline angle.
Attach the cable handles to the high pulleys of a cable machine.
Sit on the stability ball facing away from the machine, with your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Grip the cable handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Lean forward slightly, while keeping your back straight and core engaged.
With a steady motion, bring your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Continue the motion until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable incline pushdown
instructions: Lie on incline an bench facing away from a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attachment on it.

Grasp the straight bar attachment overhead with a pronated (overhand; palms down) shoulder width grip and extend your arms in front of you. The bar should be around 2 inches away from your upper thighs. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, lift your arms back in a semi circle until the bar is straight over your head. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
Slowly go back to the starting position using your lats and hold the contraction once you reach the starting position. Breathe out during the execution of this movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable incline triceps extension
instructions: Lie on incline an bench facing away from a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attachment on it.

Grasp the straight bar attachment overhead with a pronated (overhand; palms down) narrow grip (less than shoulder width) and keep your elbows tucked in to your sides. Your upper arms should create around a 25 degree angle when measured from the floor.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, extend the arms as you flex the triceps. Breathe out during this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable judo flip
instructions: Connect a rope attachment to a tower, and move the cable to the lowest pulley position. Stand with your side to the cable with a wide stance, and grab the rope with both hands.
Twist your body away from the pulley as you bring the rope over your shoulder like you're performing a judo flip.
Shift your weight between your feet as you twist and crunch forward, pulling the cable downward.
Return to the starting position and repeat until failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.

name: cable kickback
instructions: Hook a leather ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and then attach the cuff to your ankle.
Face the weight stack from a distance of about two feet, grasping the steel frame for support.

While keeping your knees and hips bent slightly and your abs tight, contract your glutes to slowly "kick" the working leg back in a semicircular arc as high as it will comfortably go as you breathe out. Tip: At full extension, squeeze your glutes for a second in order to achieve a peak contraction.
Now slowly bring your working leg forward, resisting the pull of the cable until you reach the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the movement for the other side.

name: cable kneeling crunch
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a high pulley and kneel down facing away from the machine.
Hold the rope handle with both hands and place it behind your head, while keeping your elbows out to the sides.
While keeping your hips stationary, flex your waist and crunch your upper body down towards your thighs.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable kneeling rear delt row (with rope) (male)
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a low cable pulley and kneel down facing the machine.
Grip the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and straighten your arms fully in front of you.
While keeping your back straight and core engaged, pull the rope towards your body by retracting your shoulder blades.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement and hold for a brief pause.
In a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable kneeling triceps extension
instructions: Place a bench sideways in front of a high pulley machine.
Hold a straight bar attachment above your head with your hands about 6 inches apart with your palms facing down.
Face away from the machine and kneel.
Place your head and the back of your upper arms on the bench. Your elbows should be bent with the forearms pointing towards the high pulley. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your upper arms close to your head at all times with the elbows in, press the bar out in a semicircular motion until the elbows are locked and your arms are parallel to the floor. Contract the triceps hard and keep this position for a second. Exhale as you perform this movement.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable lat pulldown full range of motion
instructions: Sit on the lat pulldown machine with your knees positioned under the pads.
Grip the cable bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up, maintaining a slight arch in your bring down back.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the bar back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lateral pulldown (with rope attachment)
instructions: Attach a rope attachment to the cable machine at a high stance.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the rope with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly back.
Pull the rope down towards your sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement.
In a controlled manner release the tension and allow the rope to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lateral pulldown with v-bar
instructions: Sit down on the cable pulldown machine and take hold of the v-bar attachment with an overhand grip.
Adjust the knee pad so that your thighs are secured under it.
Keep your back straight and lean back slightly.
Pull the v-bar down towards your upper chest while while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your back muscles at the bottom of the movement.
In a controlled manner go back the v-bar to the start stance and continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lateral raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and grip the cable handles with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and your core engaged.
Lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable low fly
instructions: Attach the handles to the low pulleys of a cable machine and select an appropriate weight.
Stand in the middle of the machine with your feet about shoulder width and a slight flex in your knees.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and straighten your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Maintaining control, in a controlled manner bring your arms forward in a sweeping motion, crossing them in front of your body.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, feeling the stretch in your chest muscles.
Reverse the motion and in a controlled manner go back your arms to the start stance, keeping tension on your chest muscles throughout.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable low seated row
instructions: Sit on the machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward, maintaining a slight flex in your elbows.
Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lying bicep curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Lay face up on a flat bench with your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Straighten your arms fully, while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the bar up towards your shoulders.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the bar back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lying close-grip curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Lay face up on a flat bench with your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Straighten your arms fully, while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the bar towards your chest by contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Bring down under control the bar back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lying extension pullover (with rope attachment)
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable machine and set the pulley at the highest stance.
Lay down on a bench with your head towards the cable machine.
Hold the rope with both hands and straighten your arms straight up above your chest.
While keeping your arms straight, bring down under control the rope behind your head while maintaining control.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then lift steadily the rope back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lying fly
instructions: Attach the handles to the cables and lay flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor.
Hold the handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended straight above your chest.
Keeping a slight flex in your elbows, bring down your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Hold briefly, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable lying triceps extension v. 2
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grasp the straight bar attachment of a low pulley with a narrow overhand grip. Tip: The easiest way to do this is to have someone hand you the bar as you lay down.
With your arms extended, position the bar over your torso. Your arms and your torso should create a 90-degree angle. This will be your starting position.

Lower the bar by bending at the elbow while keeping the upper arms stationary and elbows in. Go down until the bar lightly touches your forehead. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Flex the triceps as you lift the bar back to its starting position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Hold for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable middle fly
instructions: Attach cables to both sides of a cable machine at chest height.
Stand in the center of the machine with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and straighten your arms out to the sides.
Keep a slight flex in your elbows and keep a slight forward lean.
Activate your chest muscles and bring your arms forward in a sweeping motion.
Hold briefly at the center, then in a controlled manner go back your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable one arm bent over row
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Grip the cable handle with one hand, palm facing inward, and straighten your arm fully.
Pull the cable handle towards your body, while keeping your elbow close to your side, until your hand reaches your bring down chest.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner straighten your arm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable one arm curl
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the cable handle with an underhand grip, palm facing up.
Keep your elbow close to your side and in a controlled manner curl your forearm up towards your shoulder.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your forearm back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable one arm decline chest fly
instructions: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley cable machine and set the bench to a decline angle.
Lay down on the bench with your head towards the machine and take hold of the handle with your right hand.
Straighten your arm straight up above your chest, keeping a slight flex in your elbow.
With a steady motion, bring down your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Hold briefly, then reverse the motion and bring your arm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to your left arm and do it again the exercise.

name: cable one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a cable handle in one hand and straighten your arm out to the side, parallel to the ground.
Keep your elbow slightly bent and your palm facing forward.
In a controlled manner bring your arm across your body, squeezing your chest muscles.
Hold briefly at the end of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable one arm incline fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back against an incline bench.
Hold a cable handle in one hand with your arm extended and palm facing inward.
Keeping a slight flex in your elbow, bring down under control your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Hold briefly, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring your arm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable one arm incline press
instructions: Adjust the cable machine to a low pulley stance.
Sit on an incline bench facing away from the cable machine.
Grip the handle with one hand and bring it up to shoulder height.
Stance your feet firmly on the floor and keep a stable stance.
Press the handle forward and upward, extending your arm fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable one arm incline press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back resting against an incline bench.
Hold a cable handle in one hand and stance your arm at a 90-degree angle with your elbow bent.
Press the cable handle forward and upward, extending your arm fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the cable handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: cable one arm lateral bent-over
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, facing a cable machine.
Grip the handle with one hand and step back to create tension on the cable.
Flex forward at the waist, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Straighten your arm out to the side, parallel to the ground, with a slight flex in your elbow.
In a controlled manner bring your arm back to the start, maintaining control through the whole movement.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable one arm lateral raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, facing the cable machine.
Hold the cable handle with one hand, palm facing down, and stand far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable.
Keep your arm straight and lift steadily it out to the side until it is parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arm back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable one arm preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable one arm press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a cable handle in one hand and stance your arm at chest height, elbow bent.
Place your other hand on your hip for stability.
Press the cable handle forward, extending your arm fully.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable one arm pulldown
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the handle with an overhand grip and straighten your arm fully.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the handle down towards your side while while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your lat muscle.
In a controlled manner release the handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.
Switch sides and do it again the exercise with the other arm.

name: cable one arm reverse preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable one arm straight back high row (kneeling)
instructions: Attach a handle to a cable machine at waist height.
Kneel down facing the cable machine and take hold of the handle with one hand.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the handle towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement.
In a controlled manner release the handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.
Switch sides and do it again the exercise with the other arm.

name: cable one arm tricep pushdown
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment at chest height.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip and step back to create tension in the cable.
Stance your feet about shoulder width and slightly flex your knees.
Keep your back straight and core engaged during the exercise.
Start with your arm fully extended and perpendicular to the floor.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and push the bar down until your arm is fully extended.
Hold briefly, then breathe in and in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable overhead curl
instructions: To begin, set a weight that is comfortable on each side of the pulley machine. Note: Make sure that the amount of weight selected is the same on each side.
Now adjust the height of the pulleys on each side and make sure that they are positioned at a height higher than that of your shoulders.

Stand in the middle of both sides and use an underhand grip (palms facing towards the ceiling) to grab each handle. Your arms should be fully extended and parallel to the floor with your feet positioned shoulder width apart from each other. Your body should be evenly aligned the handles. This is the starting position.
While exhaling, slowly squeeze the biceps on each side until your forearms and biceps touch.
While inhaling, move your forearms back to the starting position. Note: Your entire body is stationary during this exercise except for the forearms.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions prescribed in your program.

name: cable overhead curl on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and hold the cable handle with an underhand grip.
Straighten your arms fully overhead, while keeping your elbows close to your ears.
In a controlled manner curl the cable down towards your forehead, while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable overhead triceps extension (rope attachment)
instructions: Sit upright on the floor with your partner behind you. Raise one arm straight up, and flex the elbow, attempting to touch your hand to your back. Your parner should hold your elbow and wrist. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to extend the arm straight into the air as your partner prevents you from doing actually doing so.
After 10-20 seconds, relax the arm and allow your partner to further stretch the tricep by applying gentle pressure to the wrist. Hold for 10-20 seconds, and then switch sides.

name: cable palm rotational row
instructions: Attach a handle to a cable machine at waist height.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the handle with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step back to create tension on the cable, while keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle towards your body, rotating your palms to face upwards as you do so.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
In a controlled manner release the handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable preacher curl
instructions: Place a preacher bench about 2 feet in front of a pulley machine.
Attach a straight bar to the low pulley.
Sit at the preacher bench with your elbow and upper arms firmly on top of the bench pad and have someone hand you the bar from the low pulley.
Grab the bar and fully extend your arms on top of the preacher bench pad. This will be your starting position.
Now start pilling the weight up towards your shoulders and squeeze the biceps hard at the top of the movement. Exhale as you perform this motion. Also, hold for a second at the top.
Now slowly lower the weight to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees at a 90-degree angle.
Hold the cable handles at chest height with your palms facing down and your elbows bent.
Activate your core and press the cable handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner release the tension and bring the cable handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable pull through (with rope)
instructions: Begin standing a few feet in front of a low pulley with a rope or handle attached. Face away from the machine, straddling the cable, with your feet set wide apart.

Begin the movement by reaching through your legs as far as possible, bending at the hips. Keep your knees slightly bent. Keeping your arms straight, extend through the hip to stand straight up. Avoid pulling upward through the shoulders; all of the motion should originate through the hips.

name: cable pulldown
instructions: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.
Grab the pull-down bar with the palms facing your torso (a supinated grip). Make sure that the hands are placed closer than the shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

As you breathe out, pull the bar down until it touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the fully contracted position and keep the elbows close to your body. The upper torso should remain stationary as your bring the bar to you and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, while breathing in, slowly bring the bar back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: cable pulldown (pro lat bar)
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your thighs are parallel to the ground and your feet are flat on the floor.
Grip the lat bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Sit down and lean back slightly, while keeping your chest up and your back straight.
Pull the bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the bar back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable pulldown bicep curl
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.
Breathe out and in a controlled manner curl the bar down towards your thighs, while keeping your wrists straight.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner go back the bar to the start stance, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable pushdown
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width and a slight flex in your knees.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.
Breathe out and push the bar down until your elbows are fully extended.
Hold briefly, then breathe in and in a controlled manner go back the bar to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable pushdown (straight arm) v. 2
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width and a slight flex in your knees.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, while keeping your arms straight and your palms facing down.
Activate your core and keep your back straight while breathing out and push the bar down towards your thighs.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then in a controlled manner go back the bar to the start stance while inhaling.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable pushdown (with rope attachment)
instructions: Attach a rope attachment to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width and a slight flex in your knees.
Grip the rope with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary during the exercise.
Breathe out and push the rope downward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly, then breathe in and in a controlled manner come back to where you began by allowing your elbows to flex.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rear delt row (stirrups)
instructions: Attach a stirrup handle to a low cable pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the handle with your left hand and take a step back with your right foot, positioning your body at a slight angle.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
With your left arm extended and your palm facing down, pull the handle towards your chest by retracting your shoulder blade.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blade.
In a controlled manner release the handle back to the start and continue for your target number of reps.
Switch sides and do it again the exercise with your right arm.

name: cable rear delt row (with rope)
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the rope handle with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and pull the rope towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rear drive
instructions: Attach a handle to a low pulley cable machine and stand facing away from the machine.
Grip the handle with an overhand grip and straighten your arms straight out in front of you.
While keeping your elbows stationary, pull the handle back towards your body, squeezing your triceps at the end of the movement.
In a controlled manner go back the handle to the start stance and continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rear pulldown
instructions: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulley is at the highest stance.
Sit facing the machine with your feet planted on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the cable attachment with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Lean back slightly, while keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Pull the cable attachment down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the cable back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable reverse crunch
instructions: Connect an ankle strap attachment to a low pulley cable and position a mat on the floor in front of it.
Sit down with your feet toward the pulley and attach the cable to your ankles.
Lie down, elevate your legs and bend your knees at a 90-degree angle. Your legs and the cable should be aligned. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are.
With your hands behind your head, bring your knees inward to your torso and elevate your hips off the floor.
Pause for a moment and in a slow and controlled manner drop your hips and bring your legs back to the starting 90-degree angle. You should still have tension on your abs in the resting position.
Repeat the same movement to failure.

name: cable reverse curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a bar attachment that is attached to a low pulley using a pronated (palms down) and shoulder width grip. Make sure also that you keep the elbows close to the torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the muscle.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable reverse grip triceps pushdown (sz-bar) (with arm blaster)
instructions: Start by setting a bar attachment (straight or e-z) on a high pulley machine.

Facing the bar attachment, grab it with the palms facing up (supinated grip) at shoulder width. Lower the bar by using your lats until your arms are fully extended by your sides. Tip: Elbows should be in by your sides and your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other. This is the starting position.
Slowly elevate the bar attachment up as you inhale so it is aligned with your chest. Only the forearms should move and the elbows/upper arms should be stationary by your side at all times.
Then begin to lower the cable bar back down to the original staring position while exhaling and contracting the triceps hard.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable reverse one arm curl
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the cable handle with an underhand grip, palm facing down.
Keep your elbow close to your side and in a controlled manner curl your forearm up towards your shoulder.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your forearm back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable reverse preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable reverse wrist curl
instructions: Attach a cable to a low pulley and sit on a bench facing the cable machine.
Grip the cable handle with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, with your wrists hanging off the edge.
While keeping your forearms stationary, breathe out and curl your wrists upward as far as possible.
Hold briefly at the top, then breathe in and bring down under control your wrists back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable reverse-grip pushdown
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands about shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary during the exercise.
Using your triceps, push the bar down until your arms are fully extended and your triceps are contracted.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner go back the bar to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable reverse-grip straight back seated high row
instructions: Sit on the seat facing the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands about shoulder width.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward from your hips.
Pull the cable towards your upper body by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles.
Hold briefly at the peak of the contraction, then in a controlled manner release the cable back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rope crossover seated row
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the cable ropes with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Lean back slightly, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable ropes towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rope elevated seated row
instructions: Sit on the elevated seat facing the cable machine.
Take hold of the cable rope handles with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly back, maintaining a slight flex in your knees.
Pull the cable towards your body by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles.
Hold briefly at the fully contracted stance.
In a controlled manner release the tension and straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rope extension incline bench row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle and attach a cable machine to the low pulley.
Attach a rope handle to the cable machine and sit on the incline bench facing the machine.
Take hold of the rope handle with an overhand grip and lean forward, while keeping your back straight.
Straighten your arms fully, pulling the rope towards your upper chest while while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
In a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rope hammer preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable rope high pulley overhead tricep extension
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and adjust the weight accordingly.
Stand facing away from the pulley machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the rope with both hands, palms facing down, and bring your hands above your head.
Keep your upper arms close to your head and perpendicular to the floor.
Bring down under control the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rope incline tricep extension
instructions: Lie on incline an bench facing away from a high pulley machine that has a straight bar attachment on it.

Grasp the straight bar attachment overhead with a pronated (overhand; palms down) narrow grip (less than shoulder width) and keep your elbows tucked in to your sides. Your upper arms should create around a 25 degree angle when measured from the floor.
Keeping the upper arms stationary, extend the arms as you flex the triceps. Breathe out during this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable rope lying on floor tricep extension
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable machine and set it to the lowest stance.
Lay on the floor facing up, with your head towards the cable machine.
Hold the rope with both hands, palms facing each other, and straighten your arms straight up towards the ceiling.
Keep your upper arms stationary and bring down under control the rope towards your forehead, bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable rope one arm hammer preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable rope seated row
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet flat on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
Grip the cable ropes with an overhand grip, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward, maintaining a slight flex in your elbows.
Pull the cable ropes towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable russian twists (on stability ball)
instructions: Connect a standard handle attachment, and position the cable to a middle pulley position.
Lie on a stability ball perpendicular to the cable and grab the handle with one hand. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable.
Grab the handle with both hands and fully extend your arms above your chest. You hands should be directly in-line with the pulley. If not, adjust the pulley up or down until they are.
Keep your hips elevated and abs engaged. Rotate your torso away from the pulley for a full-quarter rotation. Your body should be flat from head to knees.
Pause for a moment and in a slow and controlled manner reset to the starting position. You should still have side tension on the cable in the resting position.
Repeat the same movement to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.

name: cable seated chest press
instructions: Adjust the seat height and cable handles to a comfortable stance.
Sit on the bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the cable handles with an overhand grip at shoulder height.
Push the handles forward and away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner bring the handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable seated crunch
instructions: Seat on a flat bench with your back facing a high pulley.

Grasp the cable rope attachment with both hands (with the palms of the hands facing each other) and place your hands securely over both shoulders. Tip: Allow the weight to hyperextend the lower back slightly. This will be your starting position.
With the hips stationary, flex the waist so the elbows travel toward the hips. Breathe out as you perform this step.
As you inhale, go back to the initial position slowly.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable seated curl
instructions: Sit on a cable machine with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Grip the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the cable attachment towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the cable attachment back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable seated high row (v-bar)
instructions: Sit on the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the v-bar attachment with an overhand grip, palms facing each other, and your hands about shoulder width.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward from the hips.
Pull the v-bar towards your upper body by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles.
Hold briefly at the peak of the contraction, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable seated one arm alternate row
instructions: Sit on a bench facing a cable machine with your feet planted on the floor and knees slightly bent.
Grip the handle with one hand and keep your arm fully extended in front of you.
Pull the handle towards your body, retracting your shoulder blade and while keeping your elbow close to your side.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your back muscles.
In a controlled manner release the handle back to the start.
Do it again with the other arm.
Alternate between arms for your target rep count.

name: cable seated one arm concentration curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a cable handle with one hand and place your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
Keep your upper arm stationary and curl the cable handle towards your shoulder while exhaling.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Bring down under control the cable handle back to the start while inhaling.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable seated overhead curl
instructions: Sit on a bench facing the cable machine with your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands about shoulder width.
Keep your upper arms stationary and your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and curl the cable attachment towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the cable attachment back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable seated rear lateral raise
instructions: Stand in the middle of two low pulleys that are opposite to each other and place a flat bench right behind you (in perpendicular fashion to you; the narrow edge of the bench should be the one behind you). Select the weight to be used on each pulley.
Now sit at the edge of the flat bench behind you with your feet placed in front of your knees.
Bend forward while keeping your back flat and rest your torso on the thighs.

Have someone give you the single handles attached to the pulleys. Grasp the left pulley with the right hand and the right pulley with the left after you select your weight. The pulleys should run under your knees and your arms will be extended with palms facing each other and a slight bend at the elbows. This will be the starting position.

While keeping the arms stationary, raise the upper arms to the sides until they are parallel to the floor and at shoulder height. Exhale during the execution of this movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower your arms to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions. Tip: Maintain upper arms perpendicular to torso and a fixed elbow position (10 degree to 30 degree angle) throughout exercise.

name: cable seated row
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip, while keeping your back straight and your shoulders relaxed.
Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable seated shoulder internal rotation
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair facing the cable machine with your feet planted on the floor.
Hold the cable handle with your arm extended straight out in front of you, parallel to the ground.
Keep your elbow slightly bent and your shoulder blades pulled back and down.
In a controlled manner rotate your arm inward, bringing the cable handle towards the center of your body.
Hold briefly at the end of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable seated twist
instructions: Sit on a cable machine with your feet planted on the floor and your knees slightly bent.
Hold the cable handle with both hands and straighten your arms straight in front of you.
While keeping your core engaged, in a controlled manner rotate your upper body to one side, pulling the cable across your body.
Hold briefly at the end of the range of motion, then in a controlled manner rotate back to the start.
Do it again on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: cable seated wide-grip row
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the handle with a wide overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward from the hips.
Pull the handle towards your bring down chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the contraction.
In a controlled manner release the handle back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable shoulder press
instructions: Move the cables to the bottom of the towers and select an appropriate weight.
Stand directly in between the uprights. Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press the handles directly over head.
After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat.

name: cable shrug
instructions: Grasp a cable bar attachment that is attached to a low pulley with a shoulder width or slightly wider overhand (palms facing down) grip.
Stand erect close to the pulley with your arms extended in front of you holding the bar. This will be your starting position.

Lift the bar by elevating the shoulders as high as possible as you exhale. Hold the contraction at the top for a second. Tip: The arms should remain extended at all times. Refrain from using the biceps to help lift the bar. Only the shoulders should be moving up and down.
Lower the bar back to the original position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable side bend
instructions: Connect a standard handle to a tower. Move cable to highest pulley position.
Stand with side to cable. With one hand, reach up and grab handle with underhand grip.
Pull down cable until elbow touches your side and the handle is by your shoulder.
Position feet hip-width apart. Place free hand on hip to help gauge pivot point.
Keep arm in static position. Contract oblique to bring the weight down in a side crunch.
Once you reach maximum contraction, slowly release the weight to the starting position. The weight stack should never be unloaded in a resting position. The aim is constant tension during the set.
Repeat to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.

name: cable side bend crunch (bosu ball)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a cable handle in one hand.
Place the other hand on your hip.
Activate your core and in a controlled manner flex sideways towards the hand holding the cable, while keeping your back straight.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable side crunch
instructions: Attach a cable handle to a low pulley and stand sideways to the machine.
Grip the handle with the hand furthest from the machine and place your other hand on your hip.
Keep your feet about shoulder width and your knees slightly bent.
With your abs engaged, flex sideways at the waist, bringing your elbow down towards your hip.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: cable squat row (with rope attachment)
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable machine at waist height.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex your knees and bring down your body into a squat stance, while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Grip the rope with an overhand grip, with your hands about shoulder width.
Activate your core and pull the rope towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your elbows close to your body and continue pulling until your hands reach your chest.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the rope and straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable squatting curl
instructions: Attach a cable handle to the lowest setting on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the cable handle with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and arms fully extended.
Bring down your body into a squat stance, while keeping your back straight and knees behind your toes.
As you squat down, curl the cable handle towards your shoulders, while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Hold briefly at the top of the curl, squeezing your biceps.
Bring down under control the cable handle back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing back wrist curl
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the cable handle with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your arms straight and your elbows close to your sides.
In a controlled manner curl your wrists upward, bringing the cable handle towards your body.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the cable handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing calf raise
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold onto the cable machine handles or attach a cable ankle strap to your ankles.
Lift your heels off the ground by extending your ankles as high as possible.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heels back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing cross-over high reverse fly
instructions: Attach a D-handle to each side of a cable machine at shoulder height.
Stand in the middle of the cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip and straighten your arms out to the sides, palms facing forward.
Keep a slight flex in your elbows and keep a straight back during the exercise.
Activate your shoulder muscles and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles towards the front of your body.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing crunch
instructions: Attach a cable handle to a high pulley and stand facing away from the machine.
Hold the handle with both hands and place it behind your head, while keeping your elbows bent.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width and your knees slightly bent.
While keeping your abs engaged, breathe out and crunch your upper body down towards your knees, bringing your elbows towards your thighs.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing crunch (with rope attachment)
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable machine at chest height.
Stand facing away from the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the rope with both hands and bring it behind your head, while keeping your elbows bent.
Activate your abs and in a controlled manner crunch your upper body forward, bringing your elbows towards your knees.
Hold briefly at the top of the crunch, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing fly
instructions: Attach the handles to the cables at chest height.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width, facing away from the cable machine.
Grip the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Step forward slightly to create tension in the cables.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight during the exercise.
With a slight flex in your elbows, in a controlled manner bring your arms forward and together in front of your chest.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
In a controlled manner reverse the movement, returning your arms to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing hip extension
instructions: Attach a cable to a low pulley and stand facing away from the machine.
Place the cable around your ankle and stand with your feet about shoulder width.
Keep your core engaged and your back straight during the exercise.
In a controlled manner straighten your leg straight back, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Hold briefly, then come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.
Switch sides and do it again with the other leg.

name: cable standing inner curl
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the cable handle with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.
Breathe out and curl the cable handle towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the cable handle back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing lift
instructions: Connect a standard handle on a tower, and move the cable to the lowest pulley position.

With your side to the cable, grab the handle with one hand and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable. Your outstretched arm should be aligned with the cable.
