With your feet positioned shoulder width apart, squat down and grab the handle with both hands. Your arms should still be fully extended.
In one motion, pull the handle up and across your body until your arms are in a fully-extended position above your head.
Keep your back straight and your arms close to your body as you pivot your back foot and straighten your legs to get a full range of motion.
Retract your arms and then your body. Return to the neutral position in a slow and controlled manner.
Repeat to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.

name: cable standing one arm triceps extension
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, facing the cable machine.
Hold the cable handle with your right hand, palm facing down, and stance your arm so that it is fully extended and parallel to the ground.
Keep your elbow stationary and close to your body.
In a controlled manner flex your elbow, lowering the cable handle towards the back of your head.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then straighten your arm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides and do the exercise with your left arm.

name: cable standing one leg calf raise
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold onto the cable machine for support.
Lift one leg off the ground and balance on the other leg.
Lift steadily your heel off the ground, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heel back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch legs.

name: cable standing pulldown (with rope)
instructions: Attach a rope to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the rope with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your back straight and core engaged during the exercise.
Pull the rope down towards your thighs, squeezing your biceps.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then in a controlled manner release the rope back up.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing rear delt row (with rope)
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the cable attachment with both hands, palms facing each other, and step back to create tension in the cable.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the cable towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the cable back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing reverse grip one arm overhead tricep extension
instructions: Stand facing away from the cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the cable handle with an underhand grip and straighten your arm overhead, while keeping your elbow close to your head.
Keep your upper arm stationary and bring down under control the cable handle behind your head by bending your elbow.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then straighten your arm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: cable standing row (v-bar)
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the v-bar attachment with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the v-bar towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable standing shoulder external rotation
instructions: Lie sideways on a flat bench with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm. Tip: Keep the arm parallel to your torso.

Now bend the elbow while keeping the upper arm stationary. In this manner, the forearm will be parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso (Tip: So the forearm will be directly in front of you). The upper arm will be stationary by your torso and should be parallel to the floor (aligned with your torso at all times). This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted up in a semicircle motion as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the torso pointing towards the ceiling. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: cable standing twist row (v-bar)
instructions: Attach a v-bar attachment to a cable machine at chest height.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the v-bar with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Take a step back to create tension in the cable.
Keep your back straight and core engaged during the exercise.
Pull the v-bar towards your upper body by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
As you pull, twist your upper body to one side, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your upper back.
In a controlled manner release the tension and come back to where you began, untwisting your upper body.
Do it again the movement for your target rep count, alternating the twisting direction with each rep.

name: cable standing up straight crossovers
instructions: Stand in the middle of a cable machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Hold the handles of the cables with your palms facing down and your arms extended straight out to the sides.
While keeping your arms straight, bring your hands together in front of your body, crossing them over each other.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began, while keeping your arms extended.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable straight arm pulldown
instructions: You will start by grabbing the wide bar from the top pulley of a pulldown machine and using a wider than shoulder-width pronated (palms down) grip. Step backwards two feet or so.

Bend your torso forward at the waist by around 30-degrees with your arms fully extended in front of you and a slight bend at the elbows. If your arms are not fully extended then you need to step a bit more backwards until they are. Once your arms are fully extended and your torso is slightly bent at the waist, tighten the lats and then you are ready to begin.
While keeping the arms straight, pull the bar down by contracting the lats until your hands are next to the side of the thighs. Breathe out as you perform this step.
While keeping the arms straight, go back to the starting position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable straight arm pulldown (with rope)
instructions: You will start by grabbing the wide bar from the top pulley of a pulldown machine and using a wider than shoulder-width pronated (palms down) grip. Step backwards two feet or so.

Bend your torso forward at the waist by around 30-degrees with your arms fully extended in front of you and a slight bend at the elbows. If your arms are not fully extended then you need to step a bit more backwards until they are. Once your arms are fully extended and your torso is slightly bent at the waist, tighten the lats and then you are ready to begin.
While keeping the arms straight, pull the bar down by contracting the lats until your hands are next to the side of the thighs. Breathe out as you perform this step.
While keeping the arms straight, go back to the starting position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable straight back seated row
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Grip the cable handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward from the hips.
Pull the cable handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the peak of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the handles back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable supine reverse fly
instructions: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley cable machine and lay face down on a flat bench.
Grip the D-handle with each hand, palms facing down, and straighten your arms straight out in front of you.
While keeping your arms straight, lift them out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable thibaudeau kayak row
instructions: Attach a cable handle to a low pulley and sit facing the machine with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the handle with your right hand and straighten your arm fully, keeping a slight flex in your elbow.
Lean forward from your hips, while keeping your back straight and your abs engaged.
Pull the handle towards your upper body by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow, while keeping your arm close to your body.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides and do with your left arm.

name: cable triceps pushdown (v-bar)
instructions: Attach a straight or angled bar to a high pulley and grab with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width.

Standing upright with the torso straight and a very small inclination forward, bring the upper arms close to your body and perpendicular to the floor. The forearms should be pointing up towards the pulley as they hold the bar. This is your starting position.

Using the triceps, bring the bar down until it touches the front of your thighs and the arms are fully extended perpendicular to the floor. The upper arms should always remain stationary next to your torso and only the forearms should move. Exhale as you perform this movement.
After a second hold at the contracted position, bring the bar slowly up to the starting point. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable triceps pushdown (v-bar) (with arm blaster)
instructions: Attach a straight or angled bar to a high pulley and grab with an overhand grip (palms facing down) at shoulder width.

Standing upright with the torso straight and a very small inclination forward, bring the upper arms close to your body and perpendicular to the floor. The forearms should be pointing up towards the pulley as they hold the bar. This is your starting position.

Using the triceps, bring the bar down until it touches the front of your thighs and the arms are fully extended perpendicular to the floor. The upper arms should always remain stationary next to your torso and only the forearms should move. Exhale as you perform this movement.
After a second hold at the contracted position, bring the bar slowly up to the starting point. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable tuck reverse crunch
instructions: Lie down on the floor with your legs fully extended and arms to the side of your torso with the palms on the floor. Your arms should be stationary for the entire exercise.
Move your legs up so that your thighs are perpendicular to the floor and feet are together and parallel to the floor. This is the starting position.
While inhaling, move your legs towards the torso as you roll your pelvis backwards and you raise your hips off the floor. At the end of this movement your knees will be touching your chest.
Hold the contraction for a second and move your legs back to the starting position while exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable twist
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, facing the cable machine.
Hold the cable handle with both hands in front of your chest, while keeping your arms slightly bent.
Activate your core and twist your upper body to the right, pulling the cable across your body.
Hold briefly at the end of the movement, feeling the contraction in your abs and obliques.
In a controlled manner come back to where you began, resisting the cable's pull.
Do it again the movement to the left side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: cable twist (up-down)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, facing the cable machine.
Hold the cable handle with both hands in front of your chest, while keeping your arms slightly bent.
Activate your core and in a controlled manner rotate your upper body to one side, while keeping your hips and legs stable.
Hold briefly at the end of the rotation, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Do it again the rotation to the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: cable twisting pull
instructions: Attach a cable handle to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the handle with your left hand and step away from the machine, extending your arm fully.
Stance your feet about shoulder width, with your knees slightly bent.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged during the exercise.
Pull the handle towards your body, rotating your upper body to the right as you do so.
Squeeze your back muscles at the end of the movement.
In a controlled manner come back to where you began, keeping tension on the cable.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides and do with your right hand.

name: cable two arm curl on incline bench
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with your back against the pad and your feet planted on the floor.
Grip the cable handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the handles towards your shoulders while contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the handles back to the start, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable two arm tricep kickback
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and knees slightly bent.
Hold the cable handle in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, straighten your forearms backwards until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable underhand pulldown
instructions: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulldown bar is at a height above your head.
Sit down on the seat and take hold of the pulldown bar with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Keep your back straight and lean back slightly.
Pull the bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the bar back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable upper chest crossovers
instructions: Attach the handles to the cables at chest height.
Stand in the center of the cable machine with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Grip the handles with your palms facing down and your arms extended out to the sides.
Keep a slight flex in your elbows and activate your core.
Pull the cables together in front of your chest, crossing them over each other.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
In a controlled manner release the cables back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable upper row
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a cable machine at chest height.
Stand facing the machine with your feet about shoulder width.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the bar towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement.
In a controlled manner release the bar back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable upright row
instructions: Grasp a straight bar cable attachment that is attached to a low pulley with a pronated (palms facing your thighs) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The bar should be resting on top of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the cable bar as you exhale. The bar should be close to the body as you move it up. Continue to lift it until it nearly touches your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the bar, your elbows should always be higher than your forearms. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: cable wide grip rear pulldown behind neck
instructions: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulldown bar is at a height above your head.
Sit down on the seat and take hold of the pulldown bar with a wide overhand grip.
Keep your back straight and your chest up as you lean back slightly.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the movement, then in a controlled manner release the bar back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cable wrist curl
instructions: Start out by placing a flat bench in front of a low pulley cable that has a straight bar attachment.

Use your arms to grab the cable bar with a narrow to shoulder width supinated grip (palms up) and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against the top of your thighs. Your wrists should be hanging just beyond your knees.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling. Keep the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: calf push stretch with hands against wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your feet about hip width.
Place your hands against the wall at shoulder height.
Step back with one foot, while keeping your heel on the floor and your leg straight.
Flex your front knee slightly and lean forward, feeling a stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Switch legs and do it again the stretch.

name: calf stretch with hands against wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall from several feet away. Stagger your stance, placing one foot forward.
Lean forward and rest your hands on the wall, keeping your heel, hip and head in a straight line.
Attempt to keep your heel on the ground. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.

name: calf stretch with rope
instructions: Stand facing a wall or sturdy object with your feet about hip width.
Hold the ends of the rope in each hand and place the middle of the rope around the ball of your right foot.
Step back with your left foot, while keeping your heel on the floor and your leg straight.
Lean forward, while keeping your back straight, and gently pull on the rope to stretch your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release.
Do it again on the other leg.

name: cambered bar lying row
instructions: Set up a barbell on the floor and lay face down on a bench with your chest just off the edge.
Reach down and take hold of the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
With your legs straight and feet on the floor, lift the barbell off the floor by extending your arms.
Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Bring down the barbell back down to the start stance and continue for your target number of reps.

name: captains chair straight leg raise
instructions: Sit on the captain's chair with your back against the backrest and your forearms resting on the arm pads.
Keep your upper body stable and your back straight.
Activate your abs and lift your legs up in front of you, keeping them straight.
Continue lifting until your legs are parallel to the ground or as high as you can comfortably go.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: chair leg extended stretch
instructions: Sit upright in a chair and grip the seat on the sides.
Raise one leg, extending the knee, flexing the ankle as you do so.
Slowly move that leg outward as far as you can, and then back to the center and down.
Repeat for your other leg.

name: chest and front of shoulder stretch
instructions: Start off by standing with your legs together, holding a bodybar or a broomstick.
Take a slightly wider than shoulder width grip on the pole and hold it in front of you with your palms facing down.
Carefully lift the pole up and behind your head.

name: chest dip
instructions: Stance yourself on parallel bars with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Bring down your body by bending your elbows until your shoulders are below your elbows.
Push yourself back up to the start stance by straightening your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: chest dip (on dip-pull-up cage)
instructions: Adjust the dip bars to a height that allows you to comfortably grip them.
Stand between the bars and place your hands on each bar, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Jump up and straighten your arms, supporting your body weight on the bars.
Flex your knees and cross your ankles behind you.
Bring down your body by bending your elbows, while keeping your chest up and your shoulders down.
Continue lowering until your shoulders are below your elbows or until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Push through your palms and straighten your elbows to lift your body back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: chest dip on straight bar
instructions: Take hold of the parallel bars with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.
Flex your knees and cross your ankles.
Bring down your body by bending your arms until your shoulders are below your elbows.
Push yourself back up to the start stance by straightening your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: chest stretch with exercise ball
instructions: Sit on the stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold the exercise ball with both hands and straighten your arms straight out in front of you.
In a controlled manner bring the exercise ball towards your chest, feeling a stretch in your chest muscles.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: chest tap push-up (male)
instructions: Start in a high plank stance with your hands slightly wider than about shoulder width and your body in a straight line.
Bring down your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
As you bring down yourself, tap your chest with your right hand.
Push yourself back up to the start stance.
Do it again the movement, this time tapping your chest with your left hand.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: chin-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing your torso and a grip closer than the shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, keep your torso as straight as possible while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position. Tip: Keeping the torso as straight as possible maximizes biceps stimulation while minimizing back involvement.

As you breathe out, pull your torso up until your head is around the level of the pull-up bar. Concentrate on using the biceps muscles in order to perform the movement. Keep the elbows close to your body. Tip: The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.

After a second of squeezing the biceps in the contracted position, slowly lower your torso back to the starting position; when your arms are fully extended. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: chin-ups (narrow parallel grip)
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing your torso and a grip closer than the shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, keep your torso as straight as possible while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position. Tip: Keeping the torso as straight as possible maximizes biceps stimulation while minimizing back involvement.

As you breathe out, pull your torso up until your head is around the level of the pull-up bar. Concentrate on using the biceps muscles in order to perform the movement. Keep the elbows close to your body. Tip: The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.

After a second of squeezing the biceps in the contracted position, slowly lower your torso back to the starting position; when your arms are fully extended. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: circles knee stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and your hands on your hips.
Flex your knees slightly and lift your heels off the ground, balancing on the balls of your feet.
While keeping your knees bent, rotate your knees in a circular motion, first clockwise and then counterclockwise.
Do the movement for your target rep count.

name: clap push up
instructions: Start in a high plank stance with your hands slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Bring down your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, while keeping your core engaged.
Push through your palms explosively to propel your body off the ground.
While in mid-air, clap your hands together before landing back in the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: clock push-up
instructions: Move into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your hands and toes.
Your arms should be fully extended with the hands around shoulder width. Keep your body straight throughout the movement. This will be your starting position.
Descend by flexing at the elbow, lowering your chest toward the ground.
At the bottom, reverse the motion by pushing yourself up through elbow extension as quickly as possible until you are air borne. Aim to "jump" 12-18 inches to one side.
As you accelerate up, move your outside foot away from your direction of travel. Leaving the ground, shift your body about 30 degrees for the next repetition.
Return to the starting position and repeat the exercise, working all the way around until you are back where you started.

name: close grip chin-up
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing your torso and a grip closer than the shoulder width.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, keep your torso as straight as possible while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position. Tip: Keeping the torso as straight as possible maximizes biceps stimulation while minimizing back involvement.

As you breathe out, pull your torso up until your head is around the level of the pull-up bar. Concentrate on using the biceps muscles in order to perform the movement. Keep the elbows close to your body. Tip: The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.

After a second of squeezing the biceps in the contracted position, slowly lower your torso back to the starting position; when your arms are fully extended. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: close-grip push-up
instructions: Lie on the floor and place your hands on an upright dumbbell. Supporting your weight on your toes and hands, keep your torso rigid and your elbows in with your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
Lower your body, allowing the elbows to flex while you inhale. Keep your body straight, not allowing your hips to rise or sag.
Press yourself back up to the starting position by extending the elbows. Breathe out as you perform this step.
After a pause at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: close-grip push-up (on knees)
instructions: Start by getting on your hands and knees, with your hands about shoulder width and your knees about hip width.
Bring down your upper body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Hold briefly when your chest is just above the ground.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: cocoons
instructions: Begin by lying on your back on the ground. Your legs should be straight and your arms extended behind your head. This will be your starting position.

To perform the movement, tuck the knees toward your chest, rotating your pelvis to lift your glutes from the floor. As you do so, flex the spine, bringing your arms back over your head to perform a simultaneous crunch motion.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

name: crab twist toe touch
instructions: Start by sitting on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind you, fingers pointing towards your feet, and lift your hips off the ground.
Straighten one leg straight out in front of you while simultaneously reaching your opposite hand towards your toes.
Come back to where you began and do it again on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: cross body crunch
instructions: Lie flat on your back and bend your knees about 60 degrees.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and place your hands loosely behind your head. This will be your starting position.

Now curl up and bring your right elbow and shoulder across your body while bring your left knee in toward your left shoulder at the same time. Reach with your elbow and try to touch your knee. Exhale as you perform this movement. Tip: Try to bring your shoulder up towards your knee rather than just your elbow and remember that the key is to contract the abs as you perform the movement; not just to move the elbow.
Now go back down to the starting position as you inhale and repeat with the left elbow and the right knee.
Continue alternating in this manner until all prescribed repetitions are done.

name: crunch (hands overhead)
instructions: Lie on the floor with your back flat and knees bent with around a 60-degree angle between the hamstrings and the calves.
Keep your feet flat on the floor and stretch your arms overhead with your palms crossed. This will be your starting position.

Curl your upper body forward and bring your shoulder blades just off the floor. At all times, keep your arms aligned with your head, neck and shoulder. Don't move them forward from that position. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower down to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: crunch (on stability ball)
instructions: Sit on the stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Lay back on the ball until your bring down back is supported and your upper body is parallel to the floor.
Place your hands behind your head or across your chest.
Activate your abs and lift your upper body towards your knees, curling your upper body forward.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then bring down under control your upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: crunch (on stability ball, arms straight)
instructions: Sit on the stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Lay back on the ball until your bring down back is supported and your upper body is parallel to the floor.
Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Activate your abs and lift your upper body off the ball, curling your shoulders towards your hips.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: crunch floor
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your knees bent and feet planted on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Activate your abs and lift your shoulders off the ground, curling forward towards your knees.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your shoulders back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: curl-up
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your knees bent and feet planted on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
By activating your abs, lift steadily your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your upper body is at a 45-degree angle.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: curtsey squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width.
Take a step diagonally behind and across your body with your right foot, crossing it behind your left leg.
Flex both knees as if you were curtsying, lowering your body towards the ground.
Keep your upper body upright and your weight on your front foot.
Push through your front foot to come back to where you began.
Do it again on the other side, stepping diagonally behind and across your body with your left foot.

name: cycle cross trainer
instructions: Adjust the seat height and stance yourself on the cycle cross trainer.
Place your feet on the pedals and grip the handlebars.
Start pedaling in a smooth and controlled motion.
Keep a steady pace and increase the resistance if desired.
Continue pedaling for the desired duration of your cardio workout.

name: dead bug
instructions: Begin lying on your back with your hands extended above you toward the ceiling.
Bring your feet, knees, and hips up to 90 degrees.

Exhale hard to bring your ribcage down and flatten your back onto the floor, rotating your pelvis up and squeezing your glutes. Hold this position throughout the movement. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the exercise by extending one leg, straightening the knee and hip to bring the leg just above the ground.
Maintain the position of your lumbar and pelvis as you perform the movement, as your back is going to want to arch.
Stay tight and return the working leg to the starting position.
Repeat on the opposite side, alternating until the set is complete.

name: decline crunch
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down.
Now place your hands lightly on either side of your head keeping your elbows in. Tip: Don't lock your fingers behind your head.
While pushing the small of your back down in the bench to better isolate your abdominal muscles, begin to roll your shoulders off it.

Continue to push down as hard as you can with your lower back as you contract your abdominals and exhale. Your shoulders should come up off the bench only about four inches, and your lower back should remain on the bench. At the top of the movement, contract your abdominals hard and keep the contraction for a second. Tip: Focus on slow, controlled movement - don't cheat yourself by using momentum.
After the one second contraction, begin to come down slowly again to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: decline push-up
instructions: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands about 36 inches apart while holding your torso up at arms length. Move your feet up to a box or bench. This will be your starting position.
Next, lower yourself downward until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
Now breathe out and press your upper body back up to the starting position while squeezing your chest.
After a brief pause at the top contracted position, you can begin to lower yourself downward again for as many repetitions as needed.

name: decline sit-up
instructions: Lie down on the floor placing your feet either under something that will not move or by having a partner hold them. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind your head and lock them together by clasping your fingers. This is the starting position.
Elevate your upper body so that it creates an imaginary V-shape with your thighs. Breathe out when performing this part of the exercise.
Once you feel the contraction for a second, lower your upper body back down to the starting position while inhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: deep push up
instructions: Start in a high plank stance with your hands slightly wider than about shoulder width and your body in a straight line.
Bring down your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: diamond push-up
instructions: Start in a high plank stance with your hands close together, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to toe, by activating your core and glutes.
Bring down your chest towards the diamond shape formed by your hands, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: donkey calf raise
instructions: For this exercise you will need access to a donkey calf raise machine. Start by positioning your lower back and hips under the padded lever provided. The tailbone area should be the one making contact with the pad.

Place both of your arms on the side handles and place the balls of your feet on the calf block with the heels extending off. Align the toes forward, inward or outward, depending on the area you wish to target, and straighten the knees without locking them. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: drop push up
instructions: Position low boxes or other platforms 2-3 feet apart.
Move to a pushup position between them, supporting yourself by placing your hands on the boxes.
With good posture, drop from the platforms by pressing up and moving your hands to shoulder width, cushioning your landing by absorbing the impact through the arm.

name: dumbbell alternate biceps curl
instructions: Stand (torso upright) with a dumbbell in each hand held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso and the palms of your hand should be facing your thighs.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight as you rotate the palm of the hands until they are facing forward. At this point continue contracting the biceps as you breathe out until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position as your breathe in. Tip: Remember to twist the palms back to the starting position (facing your thighs) as you come down.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell alternate biceps curl (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Place the arm blaster on your upper arms, ensuring a secure fit.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Do it again the movement with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell alternate hammer preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell alternate preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell alternate seated hammer curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your upper body and arms extended down.
Keep your back straight and your elbows close to your upper body.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell in your right hand towards your shoulder, while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Continue to lift the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Pause for a brief moment, then breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Do it again the movement with your left arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell alternate side press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Press one dumbbell overhead while keeping the other dumbbell at shoulder height.
Bring down the pressed dumbbell back to shoulder height while pressing the other dumbbell overhead.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell alternating bicep curl with leg raised on exercise ball
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Place an exercise ball behind you and stance one foot on top of it, while keeping your balance.
With your arms fully extended and elbows close to your sides, curl one dumbbell towards your shoulder while while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Bring down the dumbbell back down to the start stance and do it again with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell alternating seated bicep curl on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and your arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl one dumbbell while rotating your forearm until your palm is facing your shoulder.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Do it again the curl with the other arm.
Continue alternating curls for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell arnold press
instructions: Sit on an exercise bench with back support and hold two dumbbells in front of you at about upper chest level with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent. Tip: Your arms should be next to your torso. The starting position should look like the contracted portion of a dumbbell curl.
Now to perform the movement, raise the dumbbells as you rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
Continue lifting the dumbbells until your arms are extended above you in straight arm position. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement.

After a second pause at the top, begin to lower the dumbbells to the original position by rotating the palms of your hands towards you. Tip: The left arm will be rotated in a counter clockwise manner while the right one will be rotated clockwise. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell arnold press v. 2
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing your body and elbows bent.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended and your palms are facing forward.
Rotate your wrists as you lift, so that your palms end up facing forward at the top of the movement.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell around pullover
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet firmly on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and straighten your arms straight above your chest.
While keeping your arms straight, bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head in an arc motion.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then lift the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell bench press
instructions: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other.
Then, using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells up, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. The dumbbells should be just to the sides of your chest, with your upper arm and forearm creating a 90 degree angle. Be sure to maintain full control of the dumbbells at all times. This will be your starting position.

Then, as you breathe out, use your chest to push the dumbbells up. Lock your arms at the top of the lift and squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then begin coming down slowly. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

name: dumbbell bench seated press
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Lean back and stance the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell bench squat
instructions: Place a dumbbell on the floor in front of a bench.
Stand facing away from the bench with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex at the knees and hips to bring down yourself down towards the bench, while keeping your chest up and back straight.
Once your glutes touch the bench, push through your heels to stand back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell bent over row
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, knees slightly bent, and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Flex forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Let your arms hang straight down towards the floor, with your elbows slightly bent.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell bicep curl lunge with bowling motion
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell bicep curl on exercise ball with leg raised
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell bicep curl with stork stance
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell biceps curl
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell biceps curl (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your upper body and your upper arms stationary.
Breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell biceps curl reverse
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down and arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell biceps curl squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward.
While keeping your back straight and your elbows close to your sides, breathe out and curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell biceps curl v sit on bosu ball
instructions: Sit on a bosu ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and your arms fully extended down by your sides.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell burpee
instructions: Start in a standing stance with your feet about shoulder width and a dumbbell in each hand.
Bring down your body into a squat stance, placing the dumbbells on the floor in front of you.
Kick your feet back into a push-up stance, while keeping your body in a straight line.
Do a push-up, bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the ground.
Jump your feet back towards your hands, landing in a squat stance.
Stand up explosively, lifting the dumbbells off the ground and bringing them to your shoulders.
Press the dumbbells overhead, fully extending your arms.
Bring down the dumbbells back to your shoulders and do it again the entire sequence for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell clean
instructions: Begin standing with a dumbbell in each hand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Lower the weights to the floor by flexing at the hips and knees, pushing your hips back until the dumbbells reach the floor. This will be your starting position.

To initiate the movement, violently jump upward by extending the hips, knees, and ankles to acclerate the weights upward. Maintaining a neutral grip on the dumbbells, keep the arms straight until full extension is reached.
After full extension, rebend the hips and knees to receive the weight in a squat position. Allow the arms to bend, guiding the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Upon receiving the weight in the squat position, extend the hips and knees to finish in a standing position with the weights on your shoulders.

name: dumbbell close grip press
instructions: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.

Ensuring that the dumbbell stays securely placed at the top of the bench, lie perpendicular to the bench with only your shoulders lying on the surface. Hips should be below the bench and your legs bent with your feet firmly on the floor.

Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight over your chest at arm's length. Both palms should be pressing against the underside of the sides of the dumbbell. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by lowering the dumbbell to your chest.
Return to the starting position by extending the elbows.

name: dumbbell close-grip press
instructions: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.

Ensuring that the dumbbell stays securely placed at the top of the bench, lie perpendicular to the bench with only your shoulders lying on the surface. Hips should be below the bench and your legs bent with your feet firmly on the floor.

Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight over your chest at arm's length. Both palms should be pressing against the underside of the sides of the dumbbell. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by lowering the dumbbell to your chest.
Return to the starting position by extending the elbows.

name: dumbbell concentration curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs spread apart and a dumbbell in one hand, resting your elbow on the inside of your thigh.
Fully straighten your arm and hold the dumbbell with an underhand grip.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and curl the weight up towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell contralateral forward lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Take a step forward with your right foot, while keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Bring down your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Push through your right heel to come back to where you began.
Do it again with your left leg.
Alternate legs for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell cross body hammer curl
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand. Your hands should be down at your side with your palms facing in.

While keeping your palms facing in and without twisting your arm, curl the dumbbell of the right arm up towards your left shoulder as you exhale. Touch the top of the dumbbell to your shoulder and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell along the same path as you inhale and then repeat the same movement for the left arm.
Continue alternating in this fashion until the recommended amount of repetitions is performed for each arm.

name: dumbbell cross body hammer curl v. 2
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand. Your hands should be down at your side with your palms facing in.

While keeping your palms facing in and without twisting your arm, curl the dumbbell of the right arm up towards your left shoulder as you exhale. Touch the top of the dumbbell to your shoulder and hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell along the same path as you inhale and then repeat the same movement for the left arm.
Continue alternating in this fashion until the recommended amount of repetitions is performed for each arm.

name: dumbbell cuban press
instructions: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip in a standing position. Raise your upper arms so that they are parallel to the floor, allowing your lower arms to hang in the "scarecrow" position. This will be your starting position.

To initiate the movement, externally rotate the shoulders to move the upper arm 180 degrees. Keep the upper arms in place, rotating the upper arms until the wrists are directly above the elbows, the forearms perpendicular to the floor.
Now press the dumbbells by extending at the elbows, straightening your arms overhead.
Return to the starting position as you breathe in by reversing the steps.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell cuban press v. 2
instructions: Take a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated grip in a standing position. Raise your upper arms so that they are parallel to the floor, allowing your lower arms to hang in the "scarecrow" position. This will be your starting position.

To initiate the movement, externally rotate the shoulders to move the upper arm 180 degrees. Keep the upper arms in place, rotating the upper arms until the wrists are directly above the elbows, the forearms perpendicular to the floor.
Now press the dumbbells by extending at the elbows, straightening your arms overhead.
Return to the starting position as you breathe in by reversing the steps.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell deadlift
instructions: Grasp a couple of dumbbells holding them by your side at arm's length.
Stand with your torso straight and your legs spaced using a shoulder width or narrower stance. The knees should be slightly bent. This is your starting position.

Keeping the knees stationary, lower the dumbbells to over the top of your feet by bending at the waist while keeping your back straight. Keep moving forward as if you were going to pick something from the floor until you feel a stretch on the hamstrings. Exhale as you perform this movement
Start bringing your torso up straight again by extending your hips and waist until you are back at the starting position. Inhale as you perform this movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell decline bench press
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.
Once you are laying down, move the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder width.
Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. This will be your starting position.
Bring down the weights slowly to your side as you breathe out. Keep full control of the dumbbells at all times. Tip: Throughout the motion, the forearms should always be perpendicular to the floor.

As you breathe out, push the dumbbells up using your pectoral muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up..
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

name: dumbbell decline fly
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head bring down than your hips.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Bring down the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Hold briefly, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell decline hammer press
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head bring down than your hips.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Bring down the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, while keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Press the dumbbells back up to the start stance, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell decline one arm fly
instructions: Lay down on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Using your thigh to help lift the dumbbell, lift it up to shoulder width with your palm facing your upper body.
Rotate your wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward.
As you breathe in, bring down the dumbbell in a controlled manner to the side until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Breathe out and use your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell decline one arm hammer press
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your chest.
Straighten your arm straight up, while keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Bring down the dumbbell down towards your shoulder, while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Press the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell decline shrug
instructions: Set up a decline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lay face down on the bench with your chest and stomach resting against it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended towards the floor.
While keeping your arms straight, lift your shoulders towards your ears as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell decline shrug v. 2
instructions: Set up a decline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Lay face down on the bench with your chest and stomach resting on it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms fully extended.
While keeping your arms straight, lift your shoulders as high as possible while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold the contraction for a brief pause, then bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell decline triceps extension
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.

Once you are laying down, move the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder width. The palms of the hands should be facing each other and the arms should be perpendicular to the floor and fully extended. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe in and you keep the upper arms stationary (and elbows in), bring the dumbbells down slowly by moving your forearms in a semicircular motion towards you until your thumbs are next to your ears. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Lift the dumbbells back to the starting position by contracting the triceps and exhaling.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell decline twist fly
instructions: Lay down on a decline bench with your head bring down than your hips.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended straight up over your chest.
Bring down the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
As you bring down the dumbbells, twist your wrists so that your palms face forward at the bottom of the movement.
Reverse the motion and bring the dumbbells back up to the start stance, squeezing your chest muscles at the top.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell finger curls
instructions: Hold a barbell with both hands and your palms facing up; hands spaced about shoulder width.
Place your feet flat on the floor, at a distance that is slightly wider than shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
Lower the bar as far as possible by extending the fingers. Allowing the bar to roll down the hands, catch the bar with the final joint in the fingers.
Now curl bar up as high as possible by closing your hands while exhaling. Hold the contraction at the top.

name: dumbbell fly
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down with a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.

Once you are laying down, move the dumbbells in front of you at shoulder width. The palms of the hands should be facing each other and the arms should be perpendicular to the floor and fully extended. This will be your starting position.

With a slight bend on your elbows in order to prevent stress at the biceps tendon, lower your arms out at both sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch on your chest. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Keep in mind that throughout the movement, the arms should remain stationary; the movement should only occur at the shoulder joint.
Return your arms back to the starting position as you squeeze your chest muscles and breathe out. Tip: Make sure to use the same arc of motion used to lower the weights.
Hold for a second at the contracted position and repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported by the ball.
Straighten your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other.
Flex your elbows slightly and bring down your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Hold briefly, then reverse the movement and squeeze your chest muscles as you bring the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell forward lunge triceps extension
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Take a step forward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge stance.
Keep your back straight and your chest up.
Straighten your arms straight overhead, while keeping your elbows close to your ears.
Bring down the dumbbells behind your head by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms to come back to where you began.
Do it again the movement for your target rep count, then switch legs and do it again.

name: dumbbell front raise
instructions: Pick a couple of dumbbells and stand with a straight torso and the dumbbells on front of your thighs at arms length with the palms of the hand facing your thighs. This will be your starting position.

While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the left dumbbell to the front with a slight bend on the elbow and the palms of the hands always facing down. Continue to go up until you arm is slightly above parallel to the floor. Exhale as you execute this portion of the movement and pause for a second at the top. Inhale after the second pause.
Now lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position as you simultaneously lift the right dumbbell.
Continue alternating in this fashion until all of the recommended amount of repetitions have been performed for each arm.

name: dumbbell front raise v. 2
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your thighs.
Keep your back straight and activate your core.
Lift steadily the dumbbells in front of you, with your arms straight, until they are at shoulder level.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell full can lateral raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Keep your back straight and activate your core.
Lift your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight flex in your elbows, until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell goblet squat
instructions: Stand holding a light kettlebell by the horns close to your chest. This will be your starting position.
Squat down between your legs until your hamstrings are on your calves. Keep your chest and head up and your back straight.
At the bottom position, pause and use your elbows to push your knees out. Return to the starting position, and repeat for 10-20 repetitions.

name: dumbbell hammer curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your upper body.
Keep your elbows close to your upper body and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
This will be your start stance.
Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Do it again for the recommended amount of reps.

name: dumbbell hammer curl on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and your arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the dumbbells while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell hammer curl v. 2
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your upper body.
Keep your elbows close to your upper body and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
This will be your start stance.
Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Do it again for the recommended amount of reps.

name: dumbbell hammer curls (with arm blaster)
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

Now, while holding your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the weight forward while contracting the biceps. Continue to raise the weight until the biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a brief moment as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Focus on keeping the elbow stationary and only moving your forearm.
After the brief pause, inhale and slowly begin the lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell high curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms stationary and curl the dumbbells as high as possible while contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline alternate press
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Lean back on the bench and use your thighs to help lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Once at shoulder height, rotate your wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward.
Push the dumbbells up with your chest and shoulders, extending your arms fully.
Bring down the dumbbells back down to the start stance, while keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Continue for your target number of reps, alternating arms.

name: dumbbell incline bench press
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your feet planted on the floor and your back pressed firmly against the bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward, and lift them to shoulder height.
Bring down under control the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, while keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the dumbbells back up to the start stance, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline biceps curl
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward, and arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline breeding
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Start with your arms fully extended, perpendicular to the ground.
Bring down the dumbbells in a controlled manner to the sides of your chest, while keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push the dumbbells back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline curl
instructions: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand held at arms length. Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell incline curl v. 2
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward and arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline fly
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Lay back on the bench and press the dumbbells up to the start stance, directly above your chest.
