Bring down the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Hold briefly, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline fly on exercise ball
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the incline bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Bring down the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Hold briefly, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline hammer curl
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your upper body and arms fully extended.
Keep your back against the bench and your feet flat on the floor.
While while keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline hammer press
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Lay back on the bench and stance the dumbbells at shoulder level with your palms facing each other.
Press the dumbbells up and away from your body until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline hammer press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly inward, while keeping your palms facing each other.
Straighten your arms fully, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline inner biceps curl
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on an incline bench.
The dumbbells should be at arm's length hanging at your sides and your palms should be facing out. This will be your starting position.

Now as you exhale curl the weight outward and up while keeping your forearms in line with your side deltoids. Continue the curl until the dumbbells are at shoulder height and to the sides of your deltoids. Tip: The end of the movement should look similar to a double biceps pose.
After a second contraction at the top of the movement, start to inhale and slowly lower the weights back to the starting position using the same path used to bring them up.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell incline one arm fly
instructions: Adjust the incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Lay back on the bench, while keeping your feet planted on the floor.
Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest.
Bring down the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, keeping a slight flex in your elbow.
Pause when your arm is parallel to the ground, then reverse the motion to bring the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell incline one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest, palm facing inwards.
Bring down under control the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight flex in your elbow.
Hold briefly when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Activate your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell incline one arm hammer press
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your thigh.
Lean back on the bench and use your thigh to help lift the dumbbell to shoulder height.
Rotate your wrist so that your palm is facing inward, towards your body.
Press the dumbbell up and away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell incline one arm hammer press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with your palm facing inward and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Press the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, straightening your arm.
Bring down the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell incline one arm lateral raise
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Lean forward and stance your upper arm against the inside of your thigh.
Lift the dumbbell to the side, while keeping your arm slightly bent and your palm facing down.
Continue lifting until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell incline one arm press
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your thigh.
Lay back on the bench and stance the dumbbell at shoulder level, palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward and slightly inward, extending your arm fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell incline one arm press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand, feet planted on the floor.
In a controlled manner walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell incline palm-in press
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor and keep your back straight against the bench.
Start with the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and palms facing each other.
Press the dumbbells up and away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
In a controlled manner walk your feet forward, rolling your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Press the dumbbells upward, extending your arms fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline raise
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Lean back on the bench and lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
While keeping your back against the bench, breathe out and lift the dumbbells above your head, fully extending your arms.
Hold briefly at the top, then breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline rear lateral raise
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your chest against the backrest and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Straighten your arms straight down with your palms facing each other.
Keeping a slight flex in your elbows, lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline row
instructions: Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.

name: dumbbell incline shoulder raise
instructions: Sit on an Incline Bench while holding a dumbbell on each hand on top of your thighs.

Lift your legs up to kick the weights to your shoulders and lean back. Position the dumbbells above your shoulders with your arms extended. The arms should be perpendicular to the floor with your palms facing forward and knuckles pointing towards the ceiling. This will be your starting position.
While keeping the arms straight and locked, lift the dumbbells by raising the shoulders from the bench as you breathe out.
Bring back the dumbbells to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell incline shrug
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand.
Place your feet planted on the floor and let your arms hang straight down with your palms facing your body.
While keeping your arms straight, shrug your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then bring down under control your shoulders back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline t-raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Lean forward and let your arms hang straight down, perpendicular to the floor.
While keeping your arms straight, lift them out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, forming a 'T' shape with your body.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline triceps extension
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Straighten your arms fully overhead, while keeping your elbows close to your head.
Bring down the dumbbells behind your head by bending your elbows, while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbells back to the start by extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline twisted flyes
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Lay back on the bench and press the dumbbells up to the start stance, directly above your chest, with your arms extended.
Bring down the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
As you bring down the dumbbells, rotate your wrists so that your palms face forward at the bottom of the movement.
Reverse the motion and bring the dumbbells back up to the start stance, squeezing your chest muscles together at the top.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline two arm extension
instructions: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
In a controlled manner lay back on the bench, keeping the dumbbells close to your chest.
Once you are fully lying down, straighten your arms straight up towards the ceiling, while keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell incline y-raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Lean forward slightly and let your arms hang straight down, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Lift your arms out to the sides and up in a Y shape until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell kickback
instructions: Start with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing your torso. Keep your back straight with a slight bend in the knees and bend forward at the waist. Your torso should be almost parallel to the floor. Make sure to keep your head up. Your upper arms should be close to your torso and parallel to the floor. Your forearms should be pointed towards the floor as you hold the weights. There should be a 90-degree angle formed between your forearm and upper arm. This is your starting position.
Now, while keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and use your triceps to lift the weights until the arm is fully extended. Focus on moving the forearm.
After a brief pause at the top contraction, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell kickbacks on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle.
Straighten your arms straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell kneeling bicep curl exercise ball
instructions: Kneel on the floor with an exercise ball in front of you.
Place your elbows on top of the exercise ball, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the dumbbells while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lateral raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Keep your back straight and activate your core.
Lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lateral to front raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Keep your back straight and activate your core.
Lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Next, lift your arms in front of you until they are parallel to the ground, again keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lunge
instructions: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.

Step forward with your right leg around 2 feet or so from the foot being left stationary behind and lower your upper body down, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Note: As in the other exercises, do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. Make sure that you keep your front shin perpendicular to the ground.
Using mainly the heel of your foot, push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

name: dumbbell lunge with bicep curl
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Take a step forward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge stance. Your right knee should be bent at a 90-degree angle and your left knee should be hovering just above the ground.
As you lunge forward, simultaneously curl the dumbbells towards your shoulders, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold briefly at the bottom of the lunge, then push through your right heel to come back to where you began, lowering the dumbbells back down to your sides.
Do it again the lunge and bicep curl on the opposite side, stepping forward with your left foot.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell lying extension (across face)
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and your head at the end of the bench.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and straighten your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, bring down under control the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until your forearms are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly, then squeeze your triceps to bring the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying alternate extension
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Straighten your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down one dumbbell down towards your head, bending at the elbow, while keeping the other arm extended.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then lift the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Do it again with the other arm, alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell lying elbow press
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other and arms extended straight up over your chest.
Bring down the dumbbells towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then press the dumbbells back up to the start stance by extending your elbows.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying external shoulder rotation
instructions: Lay on your side on a flat bench with your upper arm against your side and your elbow bent 90 degrees.
Hold a dumbbell in your hand with your palm facing down.
While keeping your upper arm against your side, in a controlled manner rotate your forearm upward as far as possible.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your forearm back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell lying femoral
instructions: Lay flat on your back with your legs extended and a dumbbell resting on your bring down abdomen.
Flex your knees and bring the dumbbell towards your glutes, while keeping your feet planted on the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying hammer press
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other and arms extended straight up.
Bring down the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, while keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Press the dumbbells back up to the start stance, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying on floor rear delt raise
instructions: Lay face down on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Straighten your arms straight out in front of you, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
By activating your shoulder muscles, lift your arms up and out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying one arm deltoid rear
instructions: Lay face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing inwards.
Straighten your arm straight down towards the floor, keeping it close to your body.
Lift your arm up and back, squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arm back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell lying one arm press
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet planted on the floor.
Hold the dumbbell at shoulder level with your palm facing forward.
Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell lying one arm press v. 2
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your back supported and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing towards your feet.
Straighten your arm straight up towards the ceiling, while keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Bring down under control the dumbbell down towards your chest, while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell lying one arm pronated triceps extension
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your back and head supported, and your feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing down, and straighten your arm straight up above your shoulder.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then straighten your arm back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell lying one arm rear lateral raise
instructions: While holding a dumbbell in one hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench. The other hand can be used to hold to the leg of the bench for stability.

Position the palm of the hand that is holding the dumbbell in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arm extended with the elbow slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the arm with the dumbbell to the side until your elbow is at shoulder height and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arm perpendicular to the torso while keeping your arm extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell lying one arm supinated triceps extension
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your back and head supported, and your feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, and straighten your arm straight up above your shoulder.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then straighten your arm back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell lying pronation
instructions: Lie on a flat bench face down with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm.

Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the upper arm is perpendicular to your torso. Tip: The upper arm should be parallel to the floor and also creating a 90-degree angle with your torso. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted forward as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is parallel to the floor. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell lying pronation on floor
instructions: Lie on a flat bench face down with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm.

Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the upper arm is perpendicular to your torso. Tip: The upper arm should be parallel to the floor and also creating a 90-degree angle with your torso. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted forward as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is parallel to the floor. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell lying pullover on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the ball.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and straighten your arms straight up over your chest.
Bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head while while keeping your arms straight.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying rear delt row
instructions: Lay face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Straighten your arms straight down towards the floor, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
By activating your back muscles, lift the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying rear lateral raise
instructions: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench.
Position the palms of the hands in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arms extended with the elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the arms to the side until your elbows are at shoulder height and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arms perpendicular to the torso while keeping them extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell lying single extension
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your arm fully extended above your chest.
Bring down the dumbbell in a controlled manner towards your forehead, while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then straighten your arm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell lying supination
instructions: Lie sideways on a flat bench with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm.

Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso (Tip: So the forearm will be directly in front of you). The upper arm will be stationary by your torso and should be parallel to the floor (aligned with your torso at all times). This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted up in a semicircle motion as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the torso pointing towards the ceiling. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell lying supination on floor
instructions: Lie sideways on a flat bench with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm.

Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso (Tip: So the forearm will be directly in front of you). The upper arm will be stationary by your torso and should be parallel to the floor (aligned with your torso at all times). This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted up in a semicircle motion as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the torso pointing towards the ceiling. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell lying supine biceps curl
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your back and head supported, and your feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up and your arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying supine curl
instructions: Lie down on a flat bench face up while holding a dumbbell in each arm on top of your thighs.
Bring the dumbbells to the sides with the arms extended and the palms of the hands facing your thighs (neutral grip).

While keeping the arms close to your torso and elbows in, slowly lower your arms (as you keep them extended with a slight bend at the elbows) as far down towards the floor as you can go. Once you cannot go down any further, lock your upper arms in that position and that will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, slowly begin to curl the weights up as you simultaneously rotate your wrists so that the palms of the hands face up. Continue curling the weight until your biceps are fully contracted and squeeze hard at the top position for a second. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Upper arms should remain stationary and elbows should stay in throughout the movement.
Return back to the starting position very slowly.

name: dumbbell lying triceps extension
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Straighten your arms straight up over your chest, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Bring down the dumbbells down towards your forehead, bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell lying wide curl
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up and arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell neutral grip bench press
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and your back pressed against the bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and your arms extended straight up over your chest.
Bring down under control the dumbbells down towards your chest, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push the dumbbells back up to the start stance, fully extending your arms.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell one arm bench fly
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on top of your thigh.
Lay back on the bench, keeping the dumbbell pressed against your thigh.
Using your free hand, help lift the dumbbell up to the start stance.
Hold the dumbbell directly above your shoulder with your arm extended and palm facing inward.
Bring down the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, keeping a slight flex in your elbow.
Pause when your arm is parallel to the ground, then reverse the movement and bring the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms and do it again.

name: dumbbell one arm bent-over row
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing your body.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down towards the floor, with your arm fully extended.
Pull the dumbbell up towards your chest, while keeping your elbow close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell one arm chest fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet planted on the floor.
Walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your upper back is supported on the ball and your head, neck, and shoulders are off the ball.
Straighten your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inward.
Bring down under control the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight flex in your elbow.
Hold briefly when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Activate your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm concentration curl (on stability ball)
instructions: Sit on a stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm extended down towards the floor.
Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms and do it again.

name: dumbbell one arm decline chest press
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your chest.
Place your feet planted on the floor and keep your back pressed against the bench.
Straighten your arm and push the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, fully extending your elbow.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet planted on the floor.
Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your upper back is resting on the exercise ball.
Straighten your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inwards.
Bring down under control the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight flex in your elbow.
Hold briefly, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm french press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Straighten your arm straight up towards the ceiling, while keeping your elbow stationary.
Bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm hammer preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell one arm hammer press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing inwards and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Place your other hand on your hip for stability.
Press the dumbbell upwards, extending your arm fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm incline chest press
instructions: Adjust the incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip, resting it on your shoulder.
Push the dumbbell up and away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell one arm kickback
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Bring your right elbow up to your side, keeping it bent at a 90-degree angle.
Straighten your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell one arm lateral raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing your body.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged during the exercise.
Lift the dumbbell to the side, while keeping your arm straight and your palm facing down.
Continue lifting until your arm is parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell one arm lateral raise with support
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in one hand, with your palm facing your body.
Place your other hand on a stable surface, such as a bench or wall, for support.
Keep your back straight and activate your core.
Lift the dumbbell out to the side, while keeping your arm straight and your palm facing down.
Continue lifting until your arm is parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell one arm press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and stance it at shoulder height, with your elbow bent and palm facing forward.
In a controlled manner press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended, while while keeping your core engaged and maintaining balance on the exercise ball.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell one arm prone curl
instructions: Lay face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down.
Straighten your arm fully, letting it hang straight down towards the floor.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm prone hammer curl
instructions: Lay face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing your body and arm fully extended.
Keep your upper arm stationary and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm pullover on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell with one hand and straighten your arm straight up above your chest.
Bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head while while keeping your arm straight.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm reverse wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip, palm facing down.
Rest your forearm on your thigh, with your wrist hanging off the edge.
Bring down under control the dumbbell towards the ground by flexing your wrist.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then in a controlled manner curl your wrist back up towards your body.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell one arm reverse fly (with support)
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing inwards.
Lean forward and place your free hand on the bench for support.
Keep your arm slightly bent and lift it out to the side until it is parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arm back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm reverse grip press
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing towards your body.
Place your feet planted on the floor and keep your back straight.
Lift the dumbbell to shoulder height, while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Press the dumbbell upwards until your arm is fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell one arm reverse preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell one arm reverse spider curl
instructions: Start out by setting the bar on the part of the preacher bench that you would normally sit on. Make sure to align the barbell properly so that it is balanced and will not fall off.

Move to the front side of the preacher bench (the part where the arms usually lay) and position yourself to lay at a 45 degree slant with your torso and stomach pressed against the front side of the preacher bench.
Make sure that your feet (especially the toes) are well positioned on the floor and place your upper arms on top of the pad located on the inside part of the preacher bench.
Use your arms to grab the barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing up) at about shoulder width apart or slightly closer from each other.
Slowly begin to lift the barbell upwards and exhale. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the barbell back to the starting position as your breathe in. .
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell one arm seated bicep curl on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm fully extended.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm seated hammer curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm seated neutral wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up.
Rest your forearm on your thigh, allowing your wrist to hang off the edge.
While keeping your forearm stationary, curl your wrist upward as far as possible.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your wrist back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other hand.

name: dumbbell one arm shoulder press
instructions: Grab a dumbbell and either sit on a military press bench or a utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs or stand up straight.
Clean the dumbbell up to bring it to shoulder height. The other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist or grabbing a fixed surface.
Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, push the dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended.
After a second pause, slowly come down back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm shoulder press v. 2
instructions: Grab a dumbbell and either sit on a military press bench or a utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs or stand up straight.
Clean the dumbbell up to bring it to shoulder height. The other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist or grabbing a fixed surface.
Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, push the dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended.
After a second pause, slowly come down back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm snatch
instructions: Place your feet at a shoulder width stance with the barbell resting right above the connection between the toes and the rest of the foot.

With a palms facing down grip, bend at the knees and keeping the back flat grab the bar using a wider than shoulder width grip. Bring the hips down and make sure that your body drops as if you were going to sit on a chair. This will be your starting position.
Start pushing the floor as if it were a moving platform with your feet and simultaneously start lifting the barbell keeping it close to your legs.
As the bar reaches the middle of your thighs, push the floor with your legs and lift your body to a complete extension in an explosive motion.
Lift your shoulders back in a shrugging movement as you bring the bar up while lifting your elbows out to the side and keeping them above the bar for as long as possible.

Now in a very quick but powerful motion, you have to get your body under the barbell when it has reached a high enough point where it can be controlled and drop while locking your arms and holding the barbell overhead as you assume a squat position.
Finalize the movement by rising up out of the squat position to finish the lift. At the end of the lift both feet should be on line and the arms fully extended holding the barbell overhead.

name: dumbbell one arm standing curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing forward and arm fully extended.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and curl the weight upward while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm standing hammer curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your upper body.
Keep your elbows close to your upper body and your upper arms stationary.
Breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell one arm triceps extension (on bench)
instructions: Grab a dumbbell and either sit on a military press bench or a utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs or stand up straight.

Clean the dumbbell up to bring it to shoulder height and then extend the arm over your head so that the whole arm is perpendicular to the floor and next to your head. The dumbbell should be on top of you. The other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist, supporting the upper arm that has the dumbbell or grabbing a fixed surface.
Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward and the pinkie is facing the ceiling. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head as you hold the upper arm stationary. Inhale as you perform this movement and pause when your triceps are fully stretched.
Return to the starting position by flexing your triceps as you breathe out. Tip: It is imperative that only the forearm moves. The upper arm should remain at all times stationary next to your head.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm upright row
instructions: Grab a dumbbell and stand up straight with your arm extended in front of you with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight. This will be your starting position. Tip: The dumbbell should be resting on top of your thigh with the palm of your hands facing your thighs.
Keep the other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist or grabbing a fixed surface. This will be your starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbell as you exhale. The dumbbell should be close to the body as you move it up. Continue to lift it until the dumbbell is nearly in line with your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbell, your elbow should always be higher than your forearm. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.

name: dumbbell one arm wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, resting your forearm on your thigh.
Allow your wrist to straighten, letting the dumbbell roll down towards your fingers.
In a controlled manner curl your wrist back up, bringing the dumbbell towards your forearm.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other hand.

name: dumbbell one arm zottman preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell one leg fly on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Place one foot on the floor and straighten the other leg straight out in front of you.
Lean forward slightly and bring your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down under control the dumbbells down and out to the sides, feeling a stretch in your chest.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch legs and do it again.

name: dumbbell over bench neutral wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.
Rest your forearms on the bench, allowing your wrists to hang off the edge.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Hold briefly at the top, then breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell over bench one arm neutral wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your arm extended over the bench, palm facing up.
Keep your upper arm stationary and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, while keeping your wrist in a neutral stance.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell over bench one arm reverse wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down.
Rest your forearm on the bench with your wrist hanging off the edge.
In a controlled manner curl your wrist upwards, bringing the dumbbell towards your forearm.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell over bench one arm wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down.
Rest your forearm on the bench with your wrist hanging off the edge.
In a controlled manner curl your wrist upwards, bringing the dumbbell towards your forearm.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell over bench revers wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down.
Rest your forearms on the bench, allowing your wrists to hang off the edge.
In a controlled manner curl your wrists upward, bringing the dumbbells towards your body.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell over bench wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forearms resting on the bench and your palms facing up, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Allow your wrists to hang over the edge of the bench.
In a controlled manner curl your wrists upward, squeezing your forearms at the top of the movement.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control your wrists back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell palm rotational bent over row
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Flex forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.
Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing your body.
Activate your core and pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
As you pull the dumbbells up, rotate your palms so they face away from your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance, rotating your palms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell palms in incline bench press
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back against the backrest and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing inwards.
Straighten your arms straight up above your chest, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down the dumbbells in a controlled manner towards your shoulders, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then press the dumbbells back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell peacher hammer curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your upper body.
Keep your elbows close to your upper body and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
This will be your start stance.
Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Then, breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Do it again for the recommended amount of reps.

name: dumbbell plyo squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Bring down your body into a squat stance by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
As you reach the bottom of the squat, explode upward, jumping off the ground.
While in the air, quickly switch the stance of your feet, landing with your opposite foot forward.
Immediately bring down your body back into a squat stance and do it again the jump, switching your feet again.
Continue alternating the stance of your feet with each jump for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell preacher curl
instructions: Grab a dumbbell with the right arm and place the upper arm on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbell should be held at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbell until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.

As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder height. Again, remember that to ensure full contraction you need to bring that small finger higher than the thumb.
Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the movement.

name: dumbbell preacher curl over exercise ball
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and dumbbells in each hand, resting on your thighs.
In a controlled manner walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball until your bring down back is supported on the ball and your knees are at a 90-degree angle.
Lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell pronate-grip triceps extension
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms facing down, and straighten your arms straight up overhead.
While keeping your upper arms close to your head and elbows pointing forward, bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell prone incline curl
instructions: Grab a dumbbell on each hand and lie face down on an incline bench with your shoulders near top of the incline. Your knees can rest on the seat or your legs can be straddled to the sides (my preferred way).
Let your arms extend and hang naturally in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the floor.
Now keep your elbows in by your side and face the palms forward. This will be your starting position.

Raise the dumbbells by contracting the biceps until your arms are fully flexed. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and ensure that only the forearms move. The upper arms should remain stationary at all times.
Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.

name: dumbbell prone incline hammer curl
instructions: Adjust the bench to a 45-degree incline.
Lay face down on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Allow your arms to hang straight down towards the floor, while keeping your elbows slightly bent.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell pullover
instructions: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.

Ensuring that the dumbbell stays securely placed at the top of the bench, lie perpendicular to the bench (torso across it as in forming a cross) with only your shoulders lying on the surface. Hips should be below the bench and legs bent with feet firmly on the floor. The head will be off the bench as well.

Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight over your chest with a bend in your arms. Both palms should be pressing against the underside one of the sides of the dumbbell. This will be your starting position. Caution: Always ensure that the dumbbell used for this exercise is secure. Using a dumbbell with loose plates can result in the dumbbell falling apart and falling on your face.
While keeping your arms locked in the bent arm position, lower the weight slowly in an arc behind your head while breathing in until you feel a stretch on the chest.
At that point, bring the dumbbell back to the starting position using the arc through which the weight was lowered and exhale as you perform this movement.
Hold the weight on the initial position for a second and repeat the motion for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: dumbbell pullover hip extension on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and the dumbbell resting on your thighs.
In a controlled manner walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball down your back until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Hold the dumbbell with both hands and straighten your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down the dumbbell behind your head, while keeping your arms straight and maintaining control.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbell back to the start.
While while keeping your arms extended, lift your hips off the ground, squeezing your glutes and by activating your core.
Bring down your hips back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell pullover on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms extended.
Bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head while while keeping your arms straight.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell raise
instructions: Grab a dumbbell in each arm and stand up straight with your arms extended by your sides with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight. This will be your starting position. Tip: The dumbbell should be next to your thighs with the palm of your hands facing back.

Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbells as you exhale. The dumbbells should be to the side of the body as you move them up. Continue to lift it until the dumbbells are nearly in line with your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbell, your elbow should always be higher than your forearm. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell rear delt raise
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell in each hand and with an incline bench in front of you.

While keeping your back straight and maintaining the natural arch of your back, lean forward until your forehead touches the bench in front of you. Let the arms hang in front of you perpendicular to the ground. The palms of your hands should be facing each other and your torso should be parallel to the floor. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your torso forward and stationary, and the arms straight with a slight bend at the elbows, lift the dumbbells straight to the side until both arms are parallel to the floor. Exhale as you lift the weights. Caution: avoid swinging the torso or bringing the arms back as opposed to the side.
After a one second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell rear delt row_shoulder
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and knees slightly bent.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Flex forward at the waist, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Straighten your arms straight down towards the floor, with a slight flex in your elbows.
Lift the dumbbells out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell rear fly
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Straighten your arms straight down towards the ground, palms facing each other.
Keeping a slight flex in your elbows, lift your arms out to the sides and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell rear lateral raise
instructions: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench.
Position the palms of the hands in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arms extended with the elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now raise the arms to the side until your elbows are at shoulder height and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arms perpendicular to the torso while keeping them extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell rear lateral raise (support head)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Lift your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight flex in your elbows, until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell rear lunge
instructions: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.

Step backward with your right leg around two feet or so from the left foot and lower your upper body down, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Tip: As in the other exercises, do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. Make sure that you keep your front shin perpendicular to the ground. Keep the torso upright during the lunge; flexible hip flexors are important. A long lunge emphasizes the Gluteus Maximus; a short lunge emphasizes Quadriceps.
Push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Use the ball of your feet to push in order to accentuate the quadriceps. To focus on the glutes, press with your heels.
Now repeat with the opposite leg.

name: dumbbell revers grip biceps curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down and arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell reverse bench press
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing towards your feet.
Straighten your arms straight up towards the ceiling, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down under control the dumbbells towards your chest, allowing your elbows to flare out to the sides.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push the dumbbells back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell reverse fly
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Straighten your arms straight down in front of you, palms facing each other.
Keeping a slight flex in your elbows, lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench one arm row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Place a dumbbell on the floor next to the bench.
Stand facing the bench with your feet about shoulder width.
Flex at the waist and place your left knee and left hand on the bench for support.
Pick up the dumbbell with your right hand using a reverse grip (palm facing down).
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Pull the dumbbell up towards your chest, while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Bring down the dumbbell back down to the start stance in a controlled manner.
Continue for your target number of reps.
Switch sides and do it again the exercise with your left arm.

name: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench two arm row
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your chest against the backrest and your feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Lean forward and let your arms hang straight down, fully extended.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell reverse grip row (female)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and knees slightly bent.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing your body.
Flex forward at the waist, while keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Let your arms hang straight down, fully extended, with a slight flex in your elbows.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell reverse preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell reverse spider curl
instructions: Start out by setting the bar on the part of the preacher bench that you would normally sit on. Make sure to align the barbell properly so that it is balanced and will not fall off.

Move to the front side of the preacher bench (the part where the arms usually lay) and position yourself to lay at a 45 degree slant with your torso and stomach pressed against the front side of the preacher bench.
Make sure that your feet (especially the toes) are well positioned on the floor and place your upper arms on top of the pad located on the inside part of the preacher bench.
Use your arms to grab the barbell with a supinated grip (palms facing up) at about shoulder width apart or slightly closer from each other.
Slowly begin to lift the barbell upwards and exhale. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the barbell back to the starting position as your breathe in. .
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell reverse wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with your feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang off the edge.
