In a controlled manner curl your wrists upward, bringing the dumbbells towards your body.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell romanian deadlift
instructions: Put a barbell in front of you on the ground and grab it using a pronated (palms facing down) grip that a little wider than shoulder width. Tip: Depending on the weight used, you may need wrist wraps to perform the exercise and also a raised platform in order to allow for better range of motion.
Bend the knees slightly and keep the shins vertical, hips back and back straight. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your back and arms completely straight at all times, use your hips to lift the bar as you exhale. Tip: The movement should not be fast but steady and under control.

Once you are standing completely straight up, lower the bar by pushing the hips back, only slightly bending the knees, unlike when squatting. Tip: Take a deep breath at the start of the movement and keep your chest up. Hold your breath as you lower and exhale as you complete the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell rotation reverse fly
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Lift your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight flex in your elbows, until they are parallel to the floor.
Rotate your arms so that your palms are facing downwards.
Bring down under control your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell scott press
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated alternate front raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and arms extended down by your sides.
While keeping your arms straight, lift one dumbbell in front of you until it is parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Do it again with the other arm.
Alternate between arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell seated alternate hammer curl on exercise ball
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell seated alternate press
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward.
Press one dumbbell up overhead, fully extending your arm.
Bring down the dumbbell back down to shoulder height.
Do it again with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell seated alternate shoulder
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards, and lift them to shoulder height.
Press one dumbbell up overhead while keeping the other dumbbell at shoulder height.
Bring down the raised dumbbell back to shoulder height while simultaneously pressing the other dumbbell up overhead.
Continue alternating between arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell seated bench extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and straighten your arms straight up above your head.
Bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head, while keeping your elbows close to your ears.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated bent arm lateral raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle.
While keeping your elbows bent, lift your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arms back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated bent over alternate kickback
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Flex forward at the waist, while keeping your back straight and parallel to the ground.
Straighten one arm straight back, keeping it close to your body, until your arm is fully extended.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Do it again with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell seated bent over triceps extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Flex forward at the waist, while keeping your back straight and your head up.
Straighten your arms straight back, while keeping your elbows close to your head.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated bicep curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.
Keep your back straight and your elbows close to your upper body.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated biceps curl (on stability ball)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your partner standing behind you. Extend your arms straight behind you with your palms facing each other. Your partner will hold your wrists for you. This will be the starting position.
Attempt to flex your elbows, while your partner prevents any actual movement.

After 10-20 seconds, relax your arms while your partner gently pulls your wrists up to stretch your biceps. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is appropriate to prevent injury or overstretching.

name: dumbbell seated biceps curl to shoulder press
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your partner standing behind you. Extend your arms straight behind you with your palms facing each other. Your partner will hold your wrists for you. This will be the starting position.
Attempt to flex your elbows, while your partner prevents any actual movement.

After 10-20 seconds, relax your arms while your partner gently pulls your wrists up to stretch your biceps. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is appropriate to prevent injury or overstretching.

name: dumbbell seated calf raise
instructions: Sit on the machine and place your toes on the lower portion of the platform provided with the heels extending off. Choose the toe positioning of your choice (forward, in, or out) as per the beginning of this chapter.

Place your lower thighs under the lever pad, which will need to be adjusted according to the height of your thighs. Now place your hands on top of the lever pad in order to prevent it from slipping forward.
Lift the lever slightly by pushing your heels up and release the safety bar. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower your heels by bending at the ankles until the calves are fully stretched. Inhale as you perform this movement.
Raise the heels by extending the ankles as high as possible as you contract the calves and breathe out. Hold the top contraction for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell seated curl
instructions: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell on each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights and start twisting the wrists once the dumbbells pass your thighs so that the palms of your hands face forward at the end of the movement. Make sure that you contract the biceps as you breathe out and make sure that only the forearms move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in and as you rotate the wrists back to a neutral grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell seated front raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Lift the dumbbells in front of you, with your palms facing down, until they are at shoulder level.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated hammer curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your upper body and arms extended straight down.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated inner biceps curl
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing inward in a neutral position. This will be your starting position.
While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the dumbbells out and up, turning the palms out as you lift and keeping your forearms in line with your outer deltoids. Tips:

Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in. Remember to rotate your arms as you lower the dumbbells so that you can switch back to a neutral grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell seated kickback
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Flex your knees slightly and lean forward from your hips, while keeping your back straight.
Bring your upper arms close to your sides and keep your elbows bent at a 90-degree angle.
Straighten your arms straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated lateral raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Lift the dumbbells to your sides with a slight flex in your elbows, until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated lateral raise v. 2
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Lift the dumbbells to your sides with a slight flex in your elbows, until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated neutral wrist curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing the dumbbells to hang down.
While keeping your wrists in a neutral stance, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated one arm bicep curl on exercise ball with leg raised
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm fully extended.
Place your other hand on your hip for stability.
In a controlled manner curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your bicep.
Bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.
Switch arms and do it again the exercise.

name: dumbbell seated one arm kickback
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Flex your upper body forward at the waist, while keeping your back straight and parallel to the ground.
Straighten your arm straight back, while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell seated one arm rotate
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and hold a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Lift the dumbbell up to shoulder height, while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, while while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Hold briefly at the top, then in a controlled manner rotate your forearm back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell seated one leg calf raise
instructions: Place a block on the floor about 12 inches from a flat bench.
Sit on a flat bench and place a dumbbell on your upper left thigh about 3 inches above your knee.
Now place the ball of your left foot on the block. This will be your starting position.
Raise your toes up as high as possible as you exhale and you contract your calf muscle. Hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position, stretching as far down as possible.
Repeat for your prescribed number of repetitions and then repeat with the right leg.

name: dumbbell seated one leg calf raise - hammer grip
instructions: Place a block on the floor about 12 inches from a flat bench.
Sit on a flat bench and place a dumbbell on your upper left thigh about 3 inches above your knee.
Now place the ball of your left foot on the block. This will be your starting position.
Raise your toes up as high as possible as you exhale and you contract your calf muscle. Hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position, stretching as far down as possible.
Repeat for your prescribed number of repetitions and then repeat with the right leg.

name: dumbbell seated one leg calf raise - palm up
instructions: Place a block on the floor about 12 inches from a flat bench.
Sit on a flat bench and place a dumbbell on your upper left thigh about 3 inches above your knee.
Now place the ball of your left foot on the block. This will be your starting position.
Raise your toes up as high as possible as you exhale and you contract your calf muscle. Hold the contraction for a second.
Slowly return to the starting position, stretching as far down as possible.
Repeat for your prescribed number of repetitions and then repeat with the right leg.

name: dumbbell seated palms up wrist curl
instructions: Start out by placing two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench.
Sit down on the edge of the flat bench with your legs at about shoulder width apart. Make sure to keep your feet on the floor.

Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against your thighs with the palms of the hands facing up. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge of your thighs.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.

Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling. Make sure to inhale during this part of the exercise. Tip: Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
When finished, simply lower the dumbbells to the floor.

name: dumbbell seated preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell seated revers grip concentration curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up.
Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell seated reverse grip one arm overhead tricep extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell with an underhand grip and straighten your arm straight up overhead.
Bring down the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow, while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arm back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell seated shoulder press
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated shoulder press (parallel grip)
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inward.
Lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell seated triceps extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and straighten your arms straight up overhead.
Flex your elbows and bring down the dumbbell behind your head, while keeping your upper arms close to your ears.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms and come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell shrug
instructions: Stand erect with a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing your torso), arms extended on the sides.

Lift the dumbbells by elevating the shoulders as high as possible while you exhale. Hold the contraction at the top for a second. Tip: The arms should remain extended at all times. Refrain from using the biceps to help lift the dumbbells. Only the shoulders should be moving up and down.
Lower the dumbbells back to the original position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell side bend
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on the left hand (palms facing the torso) as you have the right hand holding your waist. Your feet should be placed at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your back straight and your head up, bend only at the waist to the right as far as possible. Breathe in as you bend to the side. Then hold for a second and come back up to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Keep the rest of the body stationary.
Now repeat the movement but bending to the left instead. Hold for a second and come back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then change hands.

name: dumbbell side lying one hand raise
instructions: Lay on your side with your legs extended and your head supported by your arm.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand with your palm facing down.
While keeping your arm straight, lift the dumbbell up to shoulder height.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell side plank with rear fly
instructions: Get into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your toes and your forearms. Your arms are bent and directly below the shoulder.
Keep your body straight at all times, and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty, an arm or leg can be raised.

name: dumbbell single arm overhead carry
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Lift the dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Activate your core and keep your back straight as you walk forward, maintaining the dumbbell overhead.
Continue walking for the desired distance or time.
Switch hands and do it again the exercise.

name: dumbbell single leg calf raise
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step or platform with your heels hanging off and your toes on the step.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and place your other hand on a wall or railing for support.
Lift your heel as high as possible, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heel back down below the step.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other leg.

name: dumbbell single leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right foot slightly off the ground.
While keeping your back straight, hinge forward at the hips and bring down the dumbbell towards the ground.
At the same time, straighten your right leg straight behind you, maintaining a slight flex in your left knee.
Bring down the dumbbell until your upper body and right leg are parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly, then activate your glutes and hamstrings to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell single leg deadlift with stepbox support
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width, holding a dumbbell in your right hand.
Place your left foot on a stepbox or elevated surface behind you.
While keeping your back straight and core engaged, hinge forward at the hips, lowering the dumbbell towards the ground.
As you bring down the dumbbell, simultaneously lift your left leg behind you, maintaining a straight line from head to heel.
Bring down the dumbbell until you feel a stretch in your right hamstring, then come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell single leg split squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Take a step forward with one foot and stance your feet so that your front foot is flat on the floor and your back foot is elevated on a bench or step.
Bring down your body by bending your front knee and hip, while keeping your back knee slightly bent and your back heel off the ground.
Continue lowering until your front thigh is parallel to the ground, then push through your front heel to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch legs and do it again.

name: dumbbell single leg squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Straighten one leg forward and keep it off the ground during the exercise.
Flex your standing leg and bring down your body down as if sitting back into a chair.
Keep your chest up and your back straight.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push through your heel to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch legs.

name: dumbbell squat
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section.

Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise your torso as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing alternate hammer curl and press
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing alternate overhead press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
Press one dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Bring down the dumbbell back to shoulder level.
Do it again with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell standing alternate raise
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Lift one dumbbell to the side, while keeping your arm straight and your palm facing down.
Continue lifting until your arm is parallel to the ground.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Do it again with the other arm.
Alternate between arms for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell standing alternating tricep kickback
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Straighten your arms straight back, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Do it again with the other arm, alternating sides with each rep.

name: dumbbell standing around world
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Straighten your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.
While keeping your arms straight, in a controlled manner rotate your arms in a circular motion, bringing the dumbbells in front of your body and then overhead.
Continue the circular motion, bringing the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell standing bent over one arm triceps extension
instructions: With a dumbbell in one hand and the palm facing your torso, bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Make sure that you keep the head up.

The upper arm should be close to the torso and parallel to the floor while the forearm is pointing towards the floor as the hand holds the weight. Tip: There should be a 90-degree angle between the forearm and the upper arm. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arms stationary, use the triceps to lift the weights as you exhale until the forearms are parallel to the floor and the whole arm is extended. Like many other arm exercises, only the forearm moves.
After a second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.

name: dumbbell standing bent over two arm triceps extension
instructions: With a dumbbell in each hand and the palms facing your torso, bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward, by bending at the waist, while keeping the back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor. Make sure that you keep the head up. The upper arms should be close to the torso and parallel to the floor while the forearms are pointing towards the floor as the hands hold the weights. Tip: There should be a 90-degree angle between the forearms and the upper arm. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arms stationary, use the triceps to lift the weights as you exhale until the forearms are parallel to the floor and the whole arms are extended. Like many other arm exercises, only the forearm moves.
After a second contraction at the top, slowly lower the dumbbells back to their starting position as you inhale.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing biceps curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward and arms fully extended.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, breathe out and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and in a controlled manner begin to bring down the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell standing calf raise
instructions: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. Place the ball of the foot on a sturdy and stable wooden board (that is around 2-3 inches tall) while your heels extend off and touch the floor. This will be your starting position.

With the toes pointing either straight (to hit all parts equally), inwards (for emphasis on the outer head) or outwards (for emphasis on the inner head), raise the heels off the floor as you exhale by contracting the calves. Hold the top contraction for a second.
As you inhale, go back to the starting position by slowly lowering the heels.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.

name: dumbbell standing concentration curl
instructions: Taking a dumbbell in your working hand, lean forward. Allow your working arm to hang perpendicular to the ground with the elbow pointing out. This will be your starting position.
Flex the elbow to curl the weight, keeping the upper arm stationary. At the top of the repetition, flex the biceps and pause.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing front raise above head
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and lift the dumbbells in front of you, raising them above your head.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell standing inner biceps curl v. 2
instructions: Stand up with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso. Your legs should be at about shoulder's width apart from each other.
Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing inward in a neutral position. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights out while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Your wrist should turn so that when the weights are fully elevated you have supinated grip (palms facing up).
Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Tip: Keep the forearms aligned with your outer deltoids.
Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in. Remember to rotate the wrists as you lower the weight in order to switch back to a neutral grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing kickback
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Straighten your arms straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the dumbbells back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell standing one arm concentration curl
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up.
Place your free hand on your thigh for support.
While keeping your upper arm stationary, breathe out and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps.
Continue to lift the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted stance for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch arms.

name: dumbbell standing one arm curl (over incline bench)
instructions: Stand on the back side of an incline bench as if you were going to be a spotter for someone. Have a dumbbell in one hand and rest it across the incline bench with a supinated (palms up) grip.

Position your non lifting hand at the corner or side of the incline bench. The chest should be pressed against the top part of the incline and your feet should be pressed against the floor at a wide stance. This is the starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell upward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms while performing this exercise.

name: dumbbell standing one arm curl over incline bench
instructions: Stand on the back side of an incline bench as if you were going to be a spotter for someone. Have a dumbbell in one hand and rest it across the incline bench with a supinated (palms up) grip.

Position your non lifting hand at the corner or side of the incline bench. The chest should be pressed against the top part of the incline and your feet should be pressed against the floor at a wide stance. This is the starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell upward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms while performing this exercise.

name: dumbbell standing one arm extension
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Lift the dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Keep your upper arm close to your head and perpendicular to the ground.
Bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head, bending your elbow.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell standing one arm palm in press
instructions: Start by having a dumbbell in one hand with your arm fully extended to the side using a neutral grip. Use your other arm to hold on to an incline bench to keep your balance.

Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other. Now slowly lift the dumbbell up until you create a 90 degree angle with your arm. Note: Your forearm should be perpendicular to the floor. Continue to maintain a neutral grip throughout the entire exercise.
Slowly lift the dumbbell up until your arm is fully extended. This the starting position.
While inhaling lower the weight down until your arm is at a 90 degree angle again.

Feel the contraction for a second and then lift the weight back up towards the starting position while exhaling. Remember to hold on to the incline bench and keep your feet positioned to keep balance during the exercise.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.

name: dumbbell standing one arm reverse curl
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip.
Keep your arm fully extended and close to your body, with your palm facing down.
In a controlled manner curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder, while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell standing overhead press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to shoulder level.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell standing palms in press
instructions: Start by having a dumbbell in each hand with your arm fully extended to the side using a neutral grip. Your feet should be shoulder width apart from each other. Now slowly lift the dumbbells up until you create a 90 degree angle with your arms. Note: Your forearms should be perpendicular to the floor. This the starting position.
Continue to maintain a neutral grip throughout the entire exercise. Slowly lift the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended.
While inhaling lower the weights down until your arm is at a 90 degree angle again.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing reverse curl
instructions: To begin, stand straight with a dumbbell in each hand using a pronated grip (palms facing down). Your arms should be fully extended while your feet are shoulder width apart from each other. This is the starting position.

While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the muscle.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing triceps extension
instructions: To begin, stand up with a dumbbell held by both hands. Your feet should be about shoulder width apart from each other. Slowly use both hands to grab the dumbbell and lift it over your head until both arms are fully extended.
The resistance should be resting in the palms of your hands with your thumbs around it. The palm of the hands should be facing up towards the ceiling. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your upper arms close to your head with elbows in and perpendicular to the floor, lower the resistance in a semicircular motion behind your head until your forearms touch your biceps. Tip: The upper arms should remain stationary and only the forearms should move. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Go back to the starting position by using the triceps to raise the dumbbell. Breathe out as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell standing zottman preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell step up single leg balance with bicep curl
instructions: Stand in front of a step or platform with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Place your right foot on the step, ensuring your entire foot is in contact with the surface.
Activate your core and push through your right heel to lift your body up onto the step, bringing your left knee up towards your chest.
At the top of the movement, do a bicep curl by bending your elbows and bringing the dumbbells towards your shoulders.
Bring down the dumbbells back down and simultaneously bring down your left foot back to the ground.
Do it again the movement on the opposite side, stepping up with your left foot and curling the dumbbells.
Continue alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell step-up
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).

Place the right foot on the elevated platform. Step on the platform by extending the hip and the knee of your right leg. Use the heel mainly to lift the rest of your body up and place the foot of the left leg on the platform as well. Breathe out as you execute the force required to come up.

Step down with the left leg by flexing the hip and knee of the right leg as you inhale. Return to the original standing position by placing the right foot of to next to the left foot on the initial position.
Repeat with the right leg for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

name: dumbbell step-up lunge
instructions: Stand in front of a step or platform with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.
Place your right foot on the step, ensuring your entire foot is on the surface.
Push through your right heel and lift your body up onto the step, bringing your left foot up as well.
Once both feet are on the step, bring down your left foot back down to the start stance, while keeping your right foot on the step.
Do it again the movement, alternating which foot you step up with each time.
Continue for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell step-up split squat
instructions: Stand in front of a bench or step with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Place your right foot on the bench or step, ensuring your entire foot is in contact with the surface.
Step up onto the bench or step with your right foot, pushing through your heel to lift your body up.
As you step up, simultaneously lift your left knee towards your chest.
Pause at the top of the movement, then bring down under control your left foot back to the ground while while keeping your right foot on the bench or step.
Do it again the movement with your left foot on the bench or step.
Continue alternating between your right and left foot for your target rep count.

name: dumbbell stiff leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
While keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge at the hips and bring down the dumbbells towards the ground, allowing a slight flex in your knees.
Bring down the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then squeeze your glutes and push through your heels to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell straight arm pullover
instructions: Place a dumbbell standing up on a flat bench.

Ensuring that the dumbbell stays securely placed at the top of the bench, lie perpendicular to the bench (torso across it as in forming a cross) with only your shoulders lying on the surface. Hips should be below the bench and legs bent with feet firmly on the floor. The head will be off the bench as well.

Grasp the dumbbell with both hands and hold it straight over your chest at arms length. Both palms should be pressing against the underside one of the sides of the dumbbell. This will be your starting position.
Caution: Always ensure that the dumbbell used for this exercise is secure. Using a dumbbell with loose plates can result in the dumbbell falling apart and falling on your face.
While keeping your arms straight, lower the weight slowly in an arc behind your head while breathing in until you feel a stretch on the chest.
At that point, bring the dumbbell back to the starting position using the arc through which the weight was lowered and exhale as you perform this movement.
Hold the weight on the initial position for a second and repeat the motion for the prescribed number of repetitions.

name: dumbbell straight leg deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
While keeping your back straight and your core engaged, hinge at the hips and bring down the dumbbells towards the ground, allowing your upper body to lean forward.
Continue lowering the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, while keeping your knees slightly bent.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then activate your glutes and hamstrings to lift your upper body back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell sumo pull through
instructions: Begin standing a few feet in front of a low pulley with a rope or handle attached. Face away from the machine, straddling the cable, with your feet set wide apart.

Begin the movement by reaching through your legs as far as possible, bending at the hips. Keep your knees slightly bent. Keeping your arms straight, extend through the hip to stand straight up. Avoid pulling upward through the shoulders; all of the motion should originate through the hips.

name: dumbbell supported squat
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
While keeping your chest up and core engaged, bring down under control your body down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push through your heels to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell tate press
instructions: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand on top of your thighs. The palms of your hand will be facing each other.

By using your thighs to help you get the dumbbells up, clean the dumbbells one arm at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width. Note: when holding the dumbbells in front of you, make sure your arms are wider than shoulder width apart from each other using a pronated (palms forward) grip. Allow your elbows to point out. This is your starting position.

Keeping the upper arms stationary, slowly move the dumbbells in and down in a semi circular motion until they touch the upper chest while inhaling. Keep full control of the dumbbells at all times and do not move the upper arms nor rest the dumbbells on the chest.

As you breathe out, move the dumbbells up using your triceps and the same semi-circular motion but in reverse. Attempt to keep the dumbbells together as they move up. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down again slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

name: dumbbell tricep kickback with stork stance
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
Flex your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight.
Bring your right elbow up to your side, keeping it bent at a 90-degree angle.
Straighten your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps.
Hold briefly, then bring down under control the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps, then switch sides.

name: dumbbell twisting bench press
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and your back pressed against the bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing away from you.
Straighten your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down the dumbbells down towards your chest, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
As you bring down the dumbbells, twist your wrists so that your palms face towards you at the bottom of the movement.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then reverse the movement by pressing the dumbbells back up to the start stance.
As you press the dumbbells up, twist your wrists back to the start with palms facing away from you.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell upright row
instructions: Grasp a dumbbell in each hand with a pronated (palms forward) grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The dumbbells should be resting on top of your thighs. Your arms should be extended with a slight bend at the elbows and your back should be straight. This will be your starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbells as you exhale. The dumbbells should be close to the body as you move it up and the elbows should drive the motion. Continue to lift them until they nearly touch your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbells, your elbows should always be higher than your forearms. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell upright row (back pov)
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Let the dumbbells hang in front of your thighs, with your arms fully extended and your palms facing your body.
While keeping your back straight and your core engaged, breathe out and lift the dumbbells straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows.
Continue lifting until the dumbbells are at shoulder height, with your elbows pointing out to the sides.
Hold briefly at the top, then breathe in and bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell upright shoulder external rotation
instructions: Lie sideways on a flat bench with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.
Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm. Tip: Keep the arm parallel to your torso.

Now bend the elbow while keeping the upper arm stationary. In this manner, the forearm will be parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso (Tip: So the forearm will be directly in front of you). The upper arm will be stationary by your torso and should be parallel to the floor (aligned with your torso at all times). This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted up in a semicircle motion as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the torso pointing towards the ceiling. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.
As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: dumbbell waiter biceps curl
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms close to your body and your elbows tucked in.
In a controlled manner curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, while keeping your wrists straight.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the dumbbells back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell w-press
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Bring down the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dumbbell zottman curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
Make sure the palms of the hands are facing each other. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Your wrist should rotate so that you have a supinated (palms up) grip. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps.
Now during the contracted position, rotate your wrist until you now have a pronated (palms facing down) grip with the thumb at a higher position than the pinky.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back down using the pronated grip.
As the dumbbells close your thighs, start rotating the wrist so that you go back to a neutral (palms facing your body) grip.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbell zottman preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: dumbbells seated triceps extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in both hands with an overhand grip, and lift it above your head.
Flex your elbows and bring down the dumbbell behind your head, while keeping your upper arms close to your ears.
Straighten your arms and lift the dumbbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: dynamic chest stretch (male)
instructions: Stand with your hands together, arms extended directly in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your arms straight, quickly move your arms back as far as possible and back in again, similar to an exaggerated clapping motion. Repeat 5-10 times, increasing speed as you do so.

name: elbow dips
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge next to your hips.
Slide your hips forward off the bench and straighten your legs, while keeping your heels on the floor.
Flex your elbows and bring down your body towards the ground, while keeping your back close to the bench.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then push through your hands to straighten your arms and lift your body back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: elbow lift - reverse push-up
instructions: Start by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended and your hands placed directly under your shoulders.
Activate your core and press through your palms to lift your upper body off the ground, while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Pause at the top for a moment, squeezing your upper back muscles.
Bring down under control your body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: elbow-to-knee
instructions: Lie on the floor, crossing your right leg across your bent left knee. Clasp your hands behind your head, beginning with your shoulder blades on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Perform the motion by flexing the spine and rotating your torso to bring the left elbow to the right knee.
Return to the starting position and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

name: elevator
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and your knees slightly bent.
Place your hands on your hips or cross them in front of your chest.
While keeping your back straight, in a controlled manner flex forward at the waist, lowering your upper body towards the ground.
Hold briefly at the bottom, then lift steadily your upper body back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball alternating arm ups
instructions: Sit on the stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms extended down by your sides.
Activate your core and lift steadily one arm up towards your shoulder, while keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your arm back down to the start stance.
Do it again the movement with the other arm.
Continue alternating arms for your target rep count.

name: exercise ball back extension with arms extended
instructions: Place the stability ball on the floor and lay face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall for stability.
Straighten your arms straight out in front of you, with your palms facing down.
Activate your core and lift steadily your upper body off the ball, while keeping your back straight and your neck in line with your spine.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball back extension with hands behind head
instructions: Place the stability ball on the floor and lay face down on top of it with your hips resting on the ball.
Stance your feet against a wall or other stable surface for support.
Cross your arms behind your head, with your hands touching the back of your head.
Activate your core and lift steadily your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your hips.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, then bring down under control your upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball back extension with knees off ground
instructions: Place the stability ball on the floor and lay face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall for stability.
Stance your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Activate your core and lift steadily your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your upper body back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball back extension with rotation
instructions: Start by lying face down on the stability ball with your hips resting on the ball and your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Activate your core and lift steadily your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Hold briefly at the top, then in a controlled manner rotate your upper body to one side, while keeping your hips and legs stable.
Go back to the center and do it again the rotation to the other side.
Bring down your upper body back down to the start stance and continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball dip
instructions: Sit on the stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Place your hands on the ball beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Activate your triceps and push through your hands to lift your body off the ball, straightening your arms.
Bring down your body back down by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball hip flexor stretch
instructions: Place the stability ball on the floor and kneel in front of it.
Place your right foot on top of the stability ball, with your knee bent at a 90-degree angle.
Straighten your left leg behind you, keeping it straight.
Lean forward, pushing your hips towards the stability ball, until you feel a stretch in your right hip flexor.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides and do it again.

name: exercise ball hug
instructions: Sit on the stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold the stability ball with both hands, hugging it close to your chest.
Activate your core muscles and in a controlled manner lean back, while keeping your back straight and your feet planted on the floor.
Continue leaning back until you feel a stretch in your back muscles.
Hold the stance for a few seconds, then in a controlled manner come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball lat stretch
instructions: Sit on a stability ball with your feet planted on the floor and your back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and straighten your arm straight up overhead.
In a controlled manner lean to the opposite side, feeling a stretch in your lat muscle.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then come back to where you began.
Do it again on the other side.

name: exercise ball lower back stretch (pyramid)
instructions: Start off by rolling your torso forward onto the ball so your hips rest on top of the ball and become the highest point of your body.

Rest your hands and feet on the floor. Your arms and legs can be slightly bent or straight, depending on the size of the ball, your flexibility, and the length of your limbs. This also helps develop stabilizing strength in your torso and shoulders.

name: exercise ball lying side lat stretch
instructions: Lay on your side with your legs extended and your head supported by the stability ball.
Place your top arm on the ball for stability.
Reach your top arm overhead and allow your upper body to rotate slightly.
Feel the stretch in your lat muscles on the side of your body.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch sides and do it again.

name: exercise ball on the wall calf raise
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and place an exercise ball between your bring down back and the wall.
Stance your feet about shoulder width, with your toes pointing forward.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms extended by your sides.
Lift your heels off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heels back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball on the wall calf raise (tennis ball between ankles)
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your feet about shoulder width.
Place an exercise ball between the wall and your bring down back.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms extended by your sides.
Place a tennis ball between your ankles.
Lift your heels off the ground, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heels back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball on the wall calf raise (tennis ball between knees)
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and place an exercise ball between your bring down back and the wall.
Stance your feet about shoulder width and slightly in front of you.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms extended by your sides.
Place a tennis ball between your knees.
Lift your heels off the ground, lifting your body up onto your toes.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your heels back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball one leg prone lower body rotation
instructions: Lay face down on the stability ball with your hips resting on the ball and your legs extended straight behind you.
Place your hands on the floor in front of you for support.
Activate your glutes and core muscles to stabilize your body.
Lift steadily one leg off the ground, keeping it straight and parallel to the floor.
Rotate your leg outward, away from your body, while while keeping your hips and upper body stable.
Hold briefly at the end of the rotation, then in a controlled manner go back your leg to the start stance.
Do it again the rotation with the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for your target rep count.

name: exercise ball one legged diagonal kick hamstring curl
instructions: Start by lying on your back with your legs extended and your heels resting on top of the stability ball.
Place your arms by your sides for stability.
Activate your glutes and core muscles to lift your hips off the ground, creating a straight line from your shoulders to your heels.
Flex your right knee and bring it towards your chest, while keeping your left leg extended and your foot flexed.
Kick your right leg diagonally across your body, extending it fully and by activating your hamstrings.
In a controlled manner go back your right leg to the start stance, maintaining control and stability.
Do it again the movement with your left leg, alternating sides for your target rep count.

name: exercise ball pike push up
instructions: Start in a push-up stance with your hands on the floor and your shins resting on the stability ball.
Activate your core and lift your hips up towards the ceiling, rolling the ball towards your hands.
Keep your legs straight and your body in a pike stance, forming an inverted V shape.
Flex your elbows and bring down your upper body towards the floor, while keeping your head in line with your hands.
Push through your hands and straighten your arms to come back to where you began.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball prone leg raise
instructions: Lay face down on a mat with your legs extended and your toes resting on top of the stability ball.
Place your hands on the floor, about shoulder width, and activate your core muscles.
While keeping your legs straight, lift steadily them off the ground, using your bring down back and glutes to lift them as high as possible.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control your legs back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: exercise ball seated hamstring stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with one leg extended above you, with the hip at ninety degrees. Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
Loop a belt, band, or rope over the ball of your foot. This will be your starting position.
Pull on the belt to create tension in the calves and hamstrings. Hold this stretch for 10-30 seconds, and repeat with the other leg.

name: exercise ball seated triceps stretch
instructions: Reach your hand behind your head, grasp your elbow and gently pull. Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.

name: exercise ball supine triceps extension
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet planted on the floor and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and straighten your arms straight up towards the ceiling.
Bring down under control the dumbbell behind your head, while keeping your elbows close to your ears.
Hold briefly, then lift the dumbbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez bar french press on exercise ball
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and hold an EZ barbell with an overhand grip.
Straighten your arms straight up, while keeping your elbows close to your head.
Bring down under control the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez bar lying bent arms pullover
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Hold the EZ barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands about shoulder width.
Straighten your arms straight above your chest, keeping a slight flex in your elbows.
Bring down the barbell in an arc motion behind your head, maintaining the slight flex in your elbows.
Hold briefly, then go back the barbell to the start stance by reversing the arc motion.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez bar lying close grip triceps extension behind head
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and your head at the end of the bench.
Hold the ez barbell with a close grip, palms facing up, and straighten your arms straight up over your chest.
While keeping your upper arms stationary, bring down under control the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez bar reverse grip bent over row
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and knees slightly bent.
Hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and hands about shoulder width.
Flex forward at the hips, while keeping your back straight and chest up, until your upper body is almost parallel to the floor.
Pull the ez barbell towards your bring down chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the ez barbell back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez bar seated close grip concentration curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and hold an EZ barbell with an underhand grip.
Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
Curl the barbell up towards your shoulder while while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then bring down under control the barbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez bar standing french press
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width and hold the ez barbell with an overhand grip.
Lift the barbell above your head, fully extending your arms.
While keeping your upper arms close to your head, bring down under control the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez barbell anti gravity press
instructions: Place a bar on the ground behind the head of an incline bench.
Lay on the bench face down. With a pronated grip, pick the barbell up from the floor. Flex the elbows, performing a reverse curl to bring the bar near your chest. This will be your starting position.
To begin, press the barbell out in front of your head by extending your elbows. Keep your arms parallel to the ground throughout the movement.
Return to the starting position and repeat to complete the set.

name: ez barbell close grip preacher curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or grab the bar from the front bar rest provided by most preacher benches). The palm of your hands should be facing forward and they should be slightly tilted inwards due to the shape of the bar.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: ez barbell close-grip curl
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width and hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Keep your elbows close to your upper body and your upper arms stationary through the whole movement.
Curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then bring down under control the barbell back down to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez barbell curl
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at a shoulder-width grip. The palm of your hands should be facing forward and the elbows should be close to the torso. This will be your starting position.
While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second and squeeze the biceps hard.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: ez barbell decline close grip face press
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with your head bring down than your feet.
Grip the ez barbell with a close grip, palms facing each other.
Straighten your arms straight up above your chest, while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Bring down the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then press the barbell back up to the start stance.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez barbell decline triceps extension
instructions: Lay on a decline bench with your head bring down than your feet and your feet secured.
Hold the ez barbell with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder width.
Straighten your arms fully, while keeping your elbows close to your head.
Bring down the barbell in a controlled manner towards your forehead, bending your elbows.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez barbell incline triceps extension
instructions: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and hold the ez barbell with an overhand grip.
Straighten your arms fully overhead, while keeping your elbows close to your head.
Bring down the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows, while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Hold briefly, then straighten your arms back to the start.
Continue for your target number of reps.

name: ez barbell jm bench press
instructions: Lay flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor and your back pressed against the bench.
Grip the ez barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than about shoulder width.
Bring down the barbell to your chest, while keeping your elbows tucked in close to your body.
